There is a bowl with its mouth below and its bottom above; in it is set glory of every form.
On its rim sit seven seers; speech is the eighth, in converse with brahman.
A bowl with its mouth below and its bottom above: this is the head, for it is a bowl with its mouth below and its bottom above.
In it is set glory of every form: the prāṇas are truly glory of every form; it is the prāṇas that this means.
On its rim sit seven seers: the prāṇas are truly the seers; it is the prāṇas that this means.
Speech is the eighth, in converse with brahman: for speech is the eighth, and it converses with brahman. ॥2.2.3॥
2.2.4: These two (ears) are Gotama and Bharadvāja: this one is Gotama, this one Bharadvāja. These two (eyes) are Viśvāmitra and Jamadagni: this one is Viśvāmitra, this one Jamadagni. These two (nostrils) are Vasiṣṭha and Kaśyapa: this one is Vasiṣṭha, this one Kaśyapa. Speech is Atri, for by speech food is eaten; the name Atri is truly atti, the eater.
He who knows thus becomes the eater of all, and all becomes his food. ॥2.2.4॥
2.3.1: Brahman has just two forms: the formed and the formless, the mortal and the immortal, the fixed and the moving (yat), the definite (sat) and the beyond (tyat). ॥2.3.1॥
2.3.2: The formed is whatever is other than air and the mid-region: this is mortal, this is fixed, this is the definite (sat).
Of this formed, this mortal, this fixed, this definite, the essence is he who shines (the sun), since this is the essence of the definite. ॥2.3.2॥
2.3.3: Now the formless: air and the mid-region. This is immortal, this is the moving, this is the beyond. Of this formless, this immortal, this moving, this beyond, the essence is the person in this orb (of the sun), since this is the essence of the beyond. So much with regard to the gods. ॥2.3.3॥
2.3.4: Now with regard to the self (the body): the formed is just this, whatever is other than prāṇa, the vital breath, and this space within the body; this is mortal, this is fixed, this is the definite. Of this formed, this mortal, this fixed, this definite, the essence is the eye, since this is the essence of the definite. ॥2.3.4॥
2.3.5: Now the formless: prāṇa and this space within the body. This is immortal, this is the moving, this is the beyond. Of this formless, this immortal, this moving, this beyond, the essence is this person in the right eye, since this is the essence of the beyond. ॥2.3.5॥
2.3.6: The form of this person is this:
like a cloth dyed with turmeric, like pale white wool, like the indragopa (the red cochineal insect), like a flame of fire, like a white lotus, like a single flash of lightning.

Like a single flash of lightning is the glory of him who knows thus. Now, therefore, the teaching: not thus, not thus (neti neti); for there is no other, higher (teaching) than this: not thus. Then the name: the truth of the truth. The prāṇas are truth, and this is their truth. ॥2.3.6॥
2.4.1: Yājñavalkya said: Maitreyī, my dear, I am about to rise up from this station (the householder's life).
Come, let me make a settlement between you and Kātyāyanī here (dividing what I have). ॥2.4.1॥
2.4.2: Maitreyī said: Revered sir, if this whole earth, filled with wealth, were mine, how would I become immortal by it?
Yājñavalkya said: No. Your life would be just like the life of those who have plenty of means; but through wealth there is no hope of immortality. ॥2.4.2॥
2.4.3: Maitreyī said: What should I do with that which would not make me immortal?
Tell me just what you, revered sir, know (of the way to immortality). ॥2.4.3॥
2.4.4: Yājñavalkya said: Ah, my dear, you have been dear to us, and now you speak what is dear. Come, sit down; I shall explain it to you.
But while I explain, meditate deeply on what I say. ॥2.4.4॥
2.4.5: Yājñavalkya said: Not for the sake of the husband, my dear, is the husband dear; the husband is dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of the wife, my dear, is the wife dear; the wife is dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of sons, my dear, are sons dear; sons are dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of wealth, my dear, is wealth dear; wealth is dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of the priestly class (brahman), my dear, is the priestly class dear; the priestly class is dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of the ruling class (kṣatra), my dear, is the ruling class dear; the ruling class is dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of the worlds, my dear, are the worlds dear; the worlds are dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of the gods, my dear, are the gods dear; the gods are dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of beings, my dear, are beings dear; beings are dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of all, my dear, is all dear; all is dear for the sake of the Self. It is the Self, my dear, that is to be seen, to be heard, to be reflected on, to be meditated on.
Maitreyī, my dear, when the Self is seen, heard, reflected on and known, all this is known. ॥2.4.5॥
2.4.6: The priestly class rejects him who knows the priestly class as other than the Self; the ruling class rejects him who knows the ruling class as other than the Self; the worlds reject him who knows the worlds as other than the Self; the gods reject him who knows the gods as other than the Self; beings reject him who knows beings as other than the Self; all rejects him who knows all as other than the Self. This priestly class, this ruling class, these worlds, these gods, these beings, all this, is what this Self is. ॥2.4.6॥
2.4.7: It is as with a drum being beaten: one cannot grasp its sounds as things outside it, but by grasping the drum, or the striking of the drum, the sound is grasped. ॥2.4.7॥
2.4.8: It is as with a conch being blown: one cannot grasp its sounds as things outside it, but by grasping the conch, or the one who blows the conch, the sound is grasped. ॥2.4.8॥
2.4.9: It is as with a vīṇā being played: one cannot grasp its sounds as things outside it, but by grasping the vīṇā, or the one who plays the vīṇā, the sound is grasped. ॥2.4.9॥
2.4.10: As from a fire laid with damp fuel clouds of smoke go forth in many ways, so, my dear, the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, the Atharvāṅgirasa (the Atharvaveda), the itihāsa (histories), the purāṇa (ancient lore), the vidyās (sciences), the Upaniṣads, the ślokas (verses), the sūtras (aphorisms), the anuvyākhyānas (explanations) and the vyākhyānas (commentaries) are the breathing out of this great Being; all these are breathed out by this one alone. ॥2.4.10॥
2.4.11: As the ocean is the one place where all waters meet (ekāyana), so the skin is the one meeting place of all touches, the nose of all smells, the tongue of all tastes, the eye of all forms, the ear of all sounds, the mind of all resolves, the heart of all knowledge, the two hands of all actions, the organ of generation of all joys, the anus of all excretions, the two feet of all journeys, and speech of all the Vedas. ॥2.4.11॥
2.4.12: As a lump of salt dropped into water dissolves into the water itself, and none can take it out again, but from wherever one takes (the water), it is salt, so, my dear, this great Being, endless and boundless, is a mass of consciousness alone. Arising out of these elements, it vanishes along with them; after departing (from the body) there is no consciousness (saṃjñā). This is what I say, my dear: so said Yājñavalkya. ॥2.4.12॥
2.4.13: Maitreyī said: Just here, revered sir, you have bewildered me, (by saying that) after departing there is no consciousness.
Yājñavalkya said: I am not saying anything bewildering, my dear; this (as I have told it), my dear, is enough for understanding. ॥2.4.13॥
2.4.14: For where there is duality, as it were, there one smells another, one sees another, one hears another, one speaks to another, one thinks of another, one knows another.

But where everything has become the Self alone for him, then with what should one smell whom, with what should one see whom, with what should one hear whom, with what should one speak to whom, with what should one think of whom, with what should one know whom?
By what should one know that by which one knows all this? By what, my dear, should one know the knower? ॥2.4.14॥
2.5.1: This earth is the honey of all beings; of this earth, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this earth, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who within the body is the bodily one (śārīra): he is just this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.1॥
2.5.2: These waters are the honey of all beings; of these waters, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in these waters, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who within the body is the one in the seed (raitasa): he is just this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.2॥
2.5.3: This fire is the honey of all beings; of this fire, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this fire, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who within the body is made of speech: he is just this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.3॥
2.5.4: This air is the honey of all beings; of this air, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this air, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who within the body is prāṇa, the vital breath: he is just this Self. This is the immortal.
This is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.4॥
2.5.5: This sun is the honey of all beings; of this sun, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this sun, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who within the body is the one in the eye (cākṣuṣa): he is just this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.5॥
2.5.6: These quarters are the honey of all beings; of these quarters, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in these quarters, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who within the body is the one in the ear (śrautra), present at the time of hearing (prātiśrutka): he is just this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.6॥
2.5.7: This moon is the honey of all beings; of this moon, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this moon, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who within the body is the one in the mind (mānasa): he is just this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.7॥
2.5.8: This lightning is the honey of all beings; of this lightning, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this lightning, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who within the body is the one in the radiance of the skin (taijasa): he is just this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.8॥
2.5.9: This thunder is the honey of all beings; of this thunder, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this thunder, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who within the body is the one in sound (śābda), in the voice (sauvara): he is just this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.9॥
2.5.10: This space is the honey of all beings; of this space, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this space, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who within the body is the space in the heart: he is just this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.10॥
2.5.11: This dharma (the law of right conduct) is the honey of all beings; of this dharma, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this dharma, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who within the body is the one in dharma (dhārma): he is just this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.11॥
2.5.12: This truth is the honey of all beings; of this truth, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this truth, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who within the body is the one in truth (sātya): he is just this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.12॥
2.5.13: This humankind is the honey of all beings; of this humankind, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this humankind, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who within the body is the human one (mānuṣa): he is just this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.13॥
2.5.14: This self is the honey of all beings; of this self, all beings are the honey. The person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this self, and the person made of light, made of immortality, who is this self: he is just this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all. ॥2.5.14॥
2.5.15: This Self is indeed the overlord of all beings, the king of all beings.
As all the spokes are held fast in the hub and in the rim of a chariot wheel, so in this Self all beings, all gods, all worlds, all prāṇas (the organs), all these selves are held fast. ॥2.5.15॥
2.5.16: This indeed is that honey which Dadhyañc, son of Atharvan, taught the Aśvins.
O men (Aśvins), that fierce deed of yours, done for gain, I make known, as thunder makes known the rain:
when Dadhyañc, son of Atharvan, taught you the honey through a horse's head. ॥2.5.16॥
2.5.17: This indeed is that honey which Dadhyañc, son of Atharvan, taught the Aśvins.
O Aśvins, you brought a horse's head to Dadhyañc, son of Atharvan.
He, keeping his word, taught you the honey of Tvaṣṭṛ, and also, O Dasras (destroyers of foes), the secret (honey). ॥2.5.17॥
2.5.18: This indeed is that honey which Dadhyañc, son of Atharvan, taught the Aśvins.
Seeing this, the seer declared: He made bodies (puras) with two feet, he made bodies with four feet.
First, having become a bird, he, the Person (puruṣa), entered the bodies.
This Person is the one who lies (puriśaya) in all the bodies (pur); there is nothing he does not cover, nothing he does not fill within. ॥2.5.18॥
2.5.19: This indeed is that honey which Dadhyañc, son of Atharvan, taught the Aśvins.
He took the likeness of every form; that is for making his own form known.
Indra goes about in many forms through his māyās (powers of illusion); for yoked to him are horses, hundreds and ten. He is the horses; he is ten, and thousands, many and endless.
That Brahman is this: with nothing before it, nothing after it, nothing within it, nothing outside it. This Self is Brahman, the perceiver of all. This is the teaching. ॥2.5.19॥
2.6.1: Now the line of teachers. Pautimāṣya received this teaching from Gaupavana, Gaupavana from Pautimāṣya, Pautimāṣya from Gaupavana, Gaupavana from Kauśika, Kauśika from Kauṇḍinya, Kauṇḍinya from Śāṇḍilya, Śāṇḍilya from Kauśika and from Gautama, Gautama ॥2.6.1॥
2.6.2: from Āgniveśya, Āgniveśya from Śāṇḍilya and from Ānabhimlāta, Ānabhimlāta from Ānabhimlāta, Ānabhimlāta from Ānabhimlāta, Ānabhimlāta from Gautama, Gautama from Saitava and Prācīnayogya, Saitava and Prācīnayogya from Pārāśarya, Pārāśarya from Bhāradvāja, Bhāradvāja from Bhāradvāja and from Gautama, Gautama from Bhāradvāja, Bhāradvāja from Pārāśarya, Pārāśarya from Vaijavāpāyana, Vaijavāpāyana from Kauśikāyani, Kauśikāyani ॥2.6.2॥
2.6.3: from Ghṛtakauśika, Ghṛtakauśika from Pārāśaryāyaṇa, Pārāśaryāyaṇa from Pārāśarya, Pārāśarya from Jātūkarṇya, Jātūkarṇya from Āsurāyaṇa and from Yāska, Āsurāyaṇa from Traivaṇi, Traivaṇi from Aupajandhani, Aupajandhani from Āsuri, Āsuri from Bhāradvāja, Bhāradvāja from Ātreya, Ātreya from Māṇṭi, Māṇṭi from Gautama, Gautama from Gautama, Gautama from Vātsya, Vātsya from Śāṇḍilya, Śāṇḍilya from Kaiśorya Kāpya, Kaiśorya Kāpya from Kumārahārita, Kumārahārita from Gālava, Gālava from Vidarbhīkauṇḍinya, Vidarbhīkauṇḍinya from Vatsanapāt Bābhrava, Vatsanapāt Bābhrava from Panthā Saubhara, Panthā Saubhara from Ayāsya Āṅgirasa, Ayāsya Āṅgirasa from Ābhūti Tvāṣṭra, Ābhūti Tvāṣṭra from Viśvarūpa Tvāṣṭra, Viśvarūpa Tvāṣṭra from the two Aśvins, the two Aśvins from Dadhyaṅ Ātharvaṇa, Dadhyaṅ Ātharvaṇa from Atharvan Daiva, Atharvan Daiva from Mṛtyu Prādhvaṃsana, Mṛtyu Prādhvaṃsana from Pradhvaṃsana, Pradhvaṃsana from Ekarṣi, Ekarṣi from Vipracitti, Vipracitti from Vyaṣṭi, Vyaṣṭi from Sanāru, Sanāru from Sanātana, Sanātana from Sanaga, Sanaga from Parameṣṭhin, Parameṣṭhin from Brahman. Brahman is self-existent. Salutation to Brahman. ॥2.6.3॥
3.1.1: Om. Janaka Vaideha, king of Videha, performed a sacrifice with many gifts to the priests.
Brāhmaṇas of the Kurus and the Pañcālas had gathered there. A desire arose in Janaka Vaideha to know: Which of these brāhmaṇas is the most learned in the Veda?
He penned in a thousand cows; to the horns of each of them ten pādas (of gold) were tied. ॥3.1.1॥
3.1.2: He said to them: Revered brāhmaṇas, let him who is the best knower of Brahman among you drive these cows away.
The brāhmaṇas did not dare. Then Yājñavalkya said to his own pupil (brahmacārin): Gentle Sāmaśravas, drive these away.
The brāhmaṇas grew angry: How can he call himself the best knower of Brahman among us? Now Janaka Vaideha had a hotṛ priest, Aśvala.
He asked Yājñavalkya: Yājñavalkya, are you then the best knower of Brahman among us?
Yājñavalkya said: We bow to the best knower of Brahman; we only want the cows.
On that ground Aśvala, the hotṛ, resolved to question him. ॥3.1.2॥
3.1.3: Aśvala said: Yājñavalkya, all this is reached by death, all this is overpowered by death; by what means does the sacrificer go free beyond the grasp of death?
Yājñavalkya said: By the hotṛ priest, by fire, by speech. Speech is the hotṛ of the sacrifice.
This speech is this fire; it is the hotṛ; it is freedom, it is complete freedom. ॥3.1.3॥
3.1.4: Aśvala said: Yājñavalkya, all this is reached by day and night, all this is overpowered by day and night; by what means does the sacrificer go free beyond the grasp of day and night? Yājñavalkya said: By the adhvaryu priest, by the eye, by the sun. The eye is the adhvaryu of the sacrifice. This eye is yonder sun; it is the adhvaryu; it is freedom, it is complete freedom. ॥3.1.4॥
3.1.5: Aśvala said: Yājñavalkya, all this is reached by the bright and the dark fortnights, all this is overpowered by the bright and the dark fortnights; by what means does the sacrificer go free beyond the grasp of the bright and the dark fortnights? Yājñavalkya said: By the udgātṛ priest, by Vāyu, the air, by prāṇa, the vital breath. Prāṇa is the udgātṛ of the sacrifice.
This prāṇa is Vāyu; it is the udgātṛ; it is freedom, it is complete freedom. ॥3.1.5॥
3.1.6: Aśvala said: Yājñavalkya, this mid-region is, as it were, without support; by what foothold does the sacrificer climb to the heavenly world? Yājñavalkya said: By the brahman priest, by the mind, by the moon. The mind is the brahman priest of the sacrifice.

This mind is yonder moon; it is the brahman priest; it is freedom, it is complete freedom. These are the atimokṣas, the ways of freedom beyond death. Now the sampads, the meditations that gain the fruit of rites through a likeness. ॥3.1.6॥
3.1.7: Aśvala said: Yājñavalkya, with how many kinds of ṛk verses will this hotṛ perform (his part) in this sacrifice today?
Aśvala asked: Which are those three?
Yājñavalkya said: The puronuvākyā (the verse recited before the offering), the yājyā (the verse recited at the offering), and, third, the śasyā (the verse of praise).
Aśvala asked: What does he win by them?
Yājñavalkya said: Whatever here has life. ॥3.1.7॥
3.1.8: Aśvala said: Yājñavalkya, how many kinds of oblations will this adhvaryu offer in this sacrifice today?
Aśvala asked: Which are those three?
Yājñavalkya said: Those that blaze up when offered, those that roar loudly when offered, and those that sink down and lie (in the ground) when offered.
Aśvala asked: What does he win by them?
Yājñavalkya said: By those that blaze up when offered he wins the world of the gods, for the world of the gods shines, as it were.
By those that roar loudly when offered he wins the world of the ancestors, for the world of the ancestors is, as it were, exceedingly (loud).
By those that sink down and lie when offered he wins the world of men, for the world of men is, as it were, below. ॥3.1.8॥
3.1.9: Aśvala said: Yājñavalkya, with how many deities does this brahman priest guard the sacrifice from the south today? Yājñavalkya said: With one.
Aśvala asked: Which is that one?
Yājñavalkya said: The mind alone. The mind is endless, the Viśvedevas (the All-gods) are endless; by it he wins an endless world. ॥3.1.9॥
3.1.10: Aśvala said: Yājñavalkya, how many stotriyā verses will this udgātṛ chant in this sacrifice today?
Aśvala asked: Which are those three?
Yājñavalkya said: The puronuvākyā, the yājyā, and, third, the śasyā. Aśvala asked: Which are those that relate to the body?
Yājñavalkya said: Prāṇa is the puronuvākyā, apāna (the downward breath) the yājyā, vyāna (the breath that pervades the body) the śasyā.
Aśvala asked: What does he win by them?
Yājñavalkya said: By the puronuvākyā he wins the world of the earth, by the yājyā the world of the mid-region, by the śasyā the world of heaven. Thereupon Aśvala, the hotṛ, fell silent. ॥3.1.10॥
3.2.1: Ārtabhāga said: Yājñavalkya, how many grahas (graspers) are there, and how many atigrahas (over-graspers)? Yājñavalkya said: Eight grahas, eight atigrahas. Ārtabhāga asked: Those eight grahas and eight atigrahas, which are they? ॥3.2.1॥
3.2.2: Yājñavalkya said: Prāṇa, the vital breath, is a graha.
It is seized by the apāna, its atigraha, for it is with the apāna that one smells odours. ॥3.2.2॥
3.2.3: It is seized by name, its atigraha, for it is with speech that one speaks names. ॥3.2.3॥
3.2.4: It is seized by taste, its atigraha, for it is with the tongue that one knows tastes. ॥3.2.4॥
3.2.5: It is seized by form, its atigraha, for it is with the eye that one sees forms. ॥3.2.5॥
3.2.6: It is seized by sound, its atigraha, for it is with the ear that one hears sounds. ॥3.2.6॥
3.2.7: It is seized by desire, its atigraha, for it is with the mind that one desires desires. ॥3.2.7॥
3.2.8: The two hands are a graha.
It is seized by work, its atigraha, for it is with the hands that one does work. ॥3.2.8॥
3.2.9: It is seized by touch, its atigraha, for it is with the skin that one feels touches.
These, then, are the eight grahas and eight atigrahas. ॥3.2.9॥
3.2.10: Ārtabhāga said: Yājñavalkya, all this is the food of death; which, then, is the deity whose food is death? Yājñavalkya said: Fire is death, and it is the food of water. One conquers death that comes again. ॥3.2.10॥
3.2.11: Ārtabhāga said: Yājñavalkya, when this man dies, do the prāṇas go up out of him, or not? Yājñavalkya said: No; they are gathered together right here. He swells, he is blown up; blown up, he lies dead. ॥3.2.11॥
3.2.12: Ārtabhāga said: Yājñavalkya, when this man dies, what does not leave him?
Yājñavalkya said: The name. The name is endless, the Viśvedevas are endless; by it he wins an endless world. ॥3.2.12॥
3.2.13: Ārtabhāga said: Yājñavalkya, when the speech of this dead man goes into fire, his prāṇa into the air, his eye into the sun, his mind into the moon, his ear into the quarters, his body into the earth, his self (ātman) into space, the hairs of his body into the plants, the hairs of his head into the trees, and his blood and semen are laid down in the waters, where then is this man? Yājñavalkya said: Gentle Ārtabhāga, give me your hand; we two alone shall know of this; this is not for the two of us (to settle) in a crowd.
The two went out and conferred together. What they spoke of was karma, action, and what they praised was karma: one becomes good by good karma, and bad by bad.
3.3.1: Bhujyu said: Yājñavalkya, we wandered among the Madras as students keeping a vow (carakas), and came to the house of Patañcala Kāpya.
He had a daughter seized by a gandharva. We asked him (the gandharva): Who are you?

When we asked him about the ends of the worlds, we then said to him: Where did the Pārikṣitas (the descendants of Parikṣit) go? Where did the Pārikṣitas go, that is what I ask you, Yājñavalkya: where did the Pārikṣitas go? ॥3.3.1॥
3.3.2: Yājñavalkya said: He surely told you: They went to the place where those who perform the horse sacrifice go.
Bhujyu asked: And where do those who perform the horse sacrifice go?

Yājñavalkya said: This world is as wide as thirty-two days' journeys of the sun's chariot; the earth, twice as wide, surrounds it on all sides; the ocean, twice as wide, surrounds the earth on all sides.

There, in between, is a space as fine as a razor's edge or a fly's wing. Indra, becoming a bird (suparṇa), handed them (the Pārikṣitas) to Vāyu, the air; Vāyu placed them in himself and led them to where those who performed the horse sacrifice were. In just this way, as it were, he (the gandharva) praised Vāyu alone. Therefore Vāyu alone is the individual (vyaṣṭi), Vāyu is the whole (samaṣṭi). He who knows thus conquers death that comes again.
3.4.1: Uṣasta said: Yājñavalkya, explain to me the immediate and direct Brahman, the Self that is within all. Yājñavalkya said: This is your Self that is within all.
Uṣasta asked: Which one, Yājñavalkya, is within all?

Yājñavalkya said: He who breathes with prāṇa, the vital breath, is your Self that is within all; he who breathes down with the apāna (the downward breath) is your Self that is within all; he who breathes through the body with the vyāna (the breath that pervades the body) is your Self that is within all; he who breathes up with the udāna (the upward breath) is your Self that is within all. This, then, is your Self that is within all. ॥3.4.1॥
3.4.2: Uṣasta Cākrāyaṇa said: Just as someone might say, That is a cow, that is a horse, so has this been pointed out by you.
Explain to me that very immediate and direct Brahman, the Self that is within all.
Yājñavalkya said: This is your Self that is within all.
Uṣasta asked: Which one, Yājñavalkya, is within all?

Yājñavalkya said: You cannot see the seer of seeing, you cannot hear the hearer of hearing, you cannot think the thinker of thinking, you cannot know the knower of knowing. This is your Self that is within all. What is other than this is afflicted. Thereupon Uṣasta Cākrāyaṇa fell silent. ॥3.4.2॥
3.5.1: Then Kahola Kauṣītakeya questioned him. Kahola said: Yājñavalkya, explain to me that very immediate and direct Brahman, the Self that is within all. Yājñavalkya said: This is your Self that is within all.
Kahola asked: Which one, Yājñavalkya, is within all?

Yājñavalkya said: He who passes beyond hunger and thirst, grief and delusion, old age and death. Knowing this very Self, brāhmaṇas rise above the desire for sons, the desire for wealth and the desire for worlds, and then go about begging alms.

For the desire for sons is itself the desire for wealth, and the desire for wealth is itself the desire for worlds; both of these are only desires. Therefore a brāhmaṇa, having fully gained learning (pāṇḍitya), should wish to abide in strength (bālya).
Having fully gained both strength and learning, he becomes a muni, a man of meditation; having fully gained both what is not silence and silence, he becomes a brāhmaṇa.
How does that brāhmaṇa live? However he may live, he is just such. What is other than this is afflicted.
3.6.1: Then Gārgī Vācaknavī questioned him. Gārgī said: Yājñavalkya, all this is woven, warp and woof, in the waters; then in what are the waters woven, warp and woof?
Yājñavalkya said: In the air, Gārgī.
Gārgī asked: Then in what is the air woven, warp and woof? Yājñavalkya said: In the worlds of the mid-region, Gārgī.
Gārgī asked: Then in what are the worlds of the mid-region woven, warp and woof?
Yājñavalkya said: In the worlds of the gandharvas, Gārgī.
Gārgī asked: Then in what are the worlds of the gandharvas woven, warp and woof? Yājñavalkya said: In the worlds of the sun, Gārgī.
Gārgī asked: Then in what are the worlds of the sun woven, warp and woof?
Yājñavalkya said: In the worlds of the moon, Gārgī.
Gārgī asked: Then in what are the worlds of the moon woven, warp and woof?
Yājñavalkya said: In the worlds of the stars, Gārgī.
Gārgī asked: Then in what are the worlds of the stars woven, warp and woof?
Yājñavalkya said: In the worlds of the gods, Gārgī.
Gārgī asked: Then in what are the worlds of the gods woven, warp and woof? Yājñavalkya said: In the worlds of Indra, Gārgī.
Gārgī asked: Then in what are the worlds of Indra woven, warp and woof?
Yājñavalkya said: In the worlds of Prajāpati, Gārgī.
Gārgī asked: Then in what are the worlds of Prajāpati woven, warp and woof?
Yājñavalkya said: In the worlds of Brahmā, Gārgī.
Gārgī asked: Then in what are the worlds of Brahmā woven, warp and woof?
Yājñavalkya said: Gārgī, do not question too far, lest your head fall off. You are questioning too far about a deity about whom one must not question too far.
Gārgī, do not question too far.
Thereupon Gārgī Vācaknavī fell silent. ॥3.6.1॥
3.7.1: Then Uddālaka Āruṇi questioned him. Uddālaka said: Yājñavalkya, we lived among the Madras in the house of Patañcala Kāpya, studying the sacrifice. His wife was seized by a gandharva.
We asked him (the gandharva): Who are you?
He said to Patañcala Kāpya and to those who studied the sacrifice: Kāpya, do you know that thread by which this world, the other world and all beings are strung together?
Patañcala Kāpya said: I do not know it, revered sir.
He said to Patañcala Kāpya and to those who studied the sacrifice: Kāpya, do you know that inner ruler who rules this world, the other world and all beings from within?
Patañcala Kāpya said: I do not know him, revered sir.

He said to Patañcala Kāpya and to those who studied the sacrifice: Kāpya, he who knows that thread and that inner ruler is a knower of Brahman, a knower of the worlds, a knower of the gods, a knower of the Vedas, a knower of beings, a knower of the Self, a knower of all. He told it to them. That I know.
If you, Yājñavalkya, without knowing that thread and that inner ruler, drive away the cows that belong to the knower of Brahman, your head will fall off.
Yājñavalkya said: I do know, Gautama, that thread and that inner ruler.
Uddālaka said: Anyone at all might say: I know, I know.
Tell it as you know it. ॥3.7.1॥
3.7.2: Yājñavalkya said: Vāyu, the air, Gautama, is that thread. By Vāyu as the thread, Gautama, this world, the other world and all beings are strung together.

Therefore, Gautama, of a man who has died they say: His limbs have come loose; for by Vāyu as the thread, Gautama, they are strung together. Uddālaka said: So it is, Yājñavalkya. Now speak of the inner ruler. ॥3.7.2॥
3.7.3: Yājñavalkya said: He who dwells in the earth, is within the earth, whom the earth does not know, of whom the earth is the body, who rules the earth from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.3॥
3.7.4: He who dwells in the waters, is within the waters, whom the waters do not know, of whom the waters are the body, who rules the waters from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.4॥
3.7.5: He who dwells in fire, is within fire, whom fire does not know, of whom fire is the body, who rules fire from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.5॥
3.7.6: He who dwells in the mid-region, is within the mid-region, whom the mid-region does not know, of whom the mid-region is the body, who rules the mid-region from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.6॥
3.7.7: He who dwells in the air, is within the air, whom the air does not know, of whom the air is the body, who rules the air from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.7॥
3.7.8: He who dwells in heaven, is within heaven, whom heaven does not know, of whom heaven is the body, who rules heaven from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.8॥
3.7.9: He who dwells in the sun, is within the sun, whom the sun does not know, of whom the sun is the body, who rules the sun from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.9॥
3.7.10: He who dwells in the quarters, is within the quarters, whom the quarters do not know, of whom the quarters are the body, who rules the quarters from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.10॥
3.7.11: He who dwells in the moon and the stars, is within the moon and the stars, whom the moon and the stars do not know, of whom the moon and the stars are the body, who rules the moon and the stars from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.11॥
3.7.12: He who dwells in space, is within space, whom space does not know, of whom space is the body, who rules space from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.12॥
3.7.13: He who dwells in darkness, is within darkness, whom darkness does not know, of whom darkness is the body, who rules darkness from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.13॥
3.7.14: He who dwells in light, is within light, whom light does not know, of whom light is the body, who rules light from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. This is with regard to the deities. Now with regard to beings. ॥3.7.14॥
3.7.15: He who dwells in all beings, is within all beings, whom all beings do not know, of whom all beings are the body, who rules all beings from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. This is with regard to beings. Now with regard to the body. ॥3.7.15॥
3.7.16: He who dwells in prāṇa, is within prāṇa, whom prāṇa does not know, of whom prāṇa is the body, who rules prāṇa from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.16॥
3.7.17: He who dwells in speech, is within speech, whom speech does not know, of whom speech is the body, who rules speech from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.17॥
3.7.18: He who dwells in the eye, is within the eye, whom the eye does not know, of whom the eye is the body, who rules the eye from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.18॥
3.7.19: He who dwells in the ear, is within the ear, whom the ear does not know, of whom the ear is the body, who rules the ear from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.19॥
3.7.20: He who dwells in the mind, is within the mind, whom the mind does not know, of whom the mind is the body, who rules the mind from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.20॥
3.7.21: He who dwells in the skin, is within the skin, whom the skin does not know, of whom the skin is the body, who rules the skin from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.21॥
3.7.22: He who dwells in the intellect (vijñāna), is within the intellect, whom the intellect does not know, of whom the intellect is the body, who rules the intellect from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. ॥3.7.22॥
3.7.23: He who dwells in semen, is within semen, whom semen does not know, of whom semen is the body, who rules semen from within, he is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal: unseen, he is the seer; unheard, the hearer; unthought, the thinker; unknown, the knower.

There is no other seer than he, no other hearer than he, no other thinker than he, no other knower than he. He is your Self, the inner ruler, the immortal. What is other than this is afflicted. Thereupon Uddālaka Āruṇi fell silent. ॥3.7.23॥
3.8.1: Then Vācaknavī (Gārgī) said: Revered brāhmaṇas, well then, I shall ask him two questions. If he answers them for me, none of you will ever defeat him in a debate about Brahman (brahmodya).
3.8.2: Gārgī said: Yājñavalkya, as a hero's son of Kāśī or of Videha would string his unstrung bow, take in his hand two reed-tipped arrows that pierce the foe through, and rise up to face him, just so have I risen to face you with two questions.
3.8.3: Gārgī said: Yājñavalkya, that which is above heaven, that which is below the earth, that which is between them, these two, heaven and earth, themselves, and what they call the past, the present and the future: in what is that woven, warp and woof? ॥3.8.3॥
3.8.4: Yājñavalkya said: Gārgī, that which is above heaven, that which is below the earth, that which is between them, these two, heaven and earth, themselves, and what they call the past, the present and the future: that is woven, warp and woof, in space. ॥3.8.4॥
3.8.5: Gārgī said: Salutation to you, Yājñavalkya, for you have resolved this question of mine. Brace yourself for the next.
3.8.6: Gārgī said: Yājñavalkya, that which is above heaven, that which is below the earth, that which is between them, these two, heaven and earth, themselves, and what they call the past, the present and the future: in what is that woven, warp and woof? ॥3.8.6॥
3.8.7: Yājñavalkya said: Gārgī, that which is above heaven, that which is below the earth, that which is between them, these two, heaven and earth, themselves, and what they call the past, the present and the future: that is woven, warp and woof, in space alone.
Gārgī asked: In what, then, is space woven, warp and woof? ॥3.8.7॥
3.8.8: Yājñavalkya said: This, Gārgī, is that Imperishable (akṣara) of which the brāhmaṇas, the knowers of Brahman, speak: it is not gross, not fine, not short, not long, not red, not moist; it is without shadow, without darkness, without air, without space, clinging to nothing; it has no taste, no smell, no eyes, no ears, no speech, no mind, no radiance, no prāṇa (the vital breath), no mouth, no measure; it has no inside and no outside; it eats nothing, and nothing eats it. ॥3.8.8॥
3.8.9: Under the rule (praśāsana) of this Imperishable, Gārgī, the sun and the moon stand held in their places; under the rule of this Imperishable, Gārgī, heaven and earth stand held in their places; under the rule of this Imperishable, Gārgī, the moments, the muhūrtas, days and nights, half-months, months, seasons and years stand held in their places; under the rule of this Imperishable, Gārgī, some rivers flow eastward from the white mountains, others westward, and others in whatever direction (each takes); under the rule of this Imperishable, Gārgī, men praise those who give, the gods depend on the sacrificer, and the ancestors on the darvī offering. ॥3.8.9॥
3.8.10: Whoever, Gārgī, without knowing this Imperishable, makes offerings in this world, sacrifices and practises austerity for many thousands of years, all that of his comes to an end; whoever, Gārgī, departs from this world without knowing this Imperishable is to be pitied (kṛpaṇa); but he who departs from this world knowing this Imperishable, Gārgī, is a brāhmaṇa. ॥3.8.10॥
3.8.11: That Imperishable, Gārgī, unseen, is the seer; unheard, the hearer; unthought, the thinker; unknown, the knower. There is no other seer than it, no other hearer than it, no other thinker than it, no other knower than it. In this Imperishable, Gārgī, is space woven, warp and woof. ॥3.8.11॥
3.8.12: Gārgī said: Revered brāhmaṇas, count it a great thing if you get free of him by bowing to him; none of you will ever defeat him in a debate about Brahman. Thereupon Vācaknavī fell silent. ॥3.8.12॥
3.9.1: Then Vidagdha Śākalya questioned him: Yājñavalkya, how many gods are there?

Yājñavalkya answered with this very nivid: As many as are named in the nivid of the Vaiśvadeva (śastra): three and three hundred, three and three thousand. Śākalya said: Om (yes). Yājñavalkya, how many gods are there in fact?
Yājñavalkya said: Thirty-three. Śākalya said: Om.
Śākalya asked: Yājñavalkya, how many gods are there in fact?
Yājñavalkya said: Six. Śākalya said: Om.
Śākalya asked: Yājñavalkya, how many gods are there in fact?
Yājñavalkya said: Three. Śākalya said: Om.
Śākalya asked: Yājñavalkya, how many gods are there in fact? Yājñavalkya said: Two. Śākalya said: Om.
Śākalya asked: Yājñavalkya, how many gods are there in fact? Yājñavalkya said: One and a half. Śākalya said: Om.
Śākalya asked: Yājñavalkya, how many gods are there in fact? Yājñavalkya said: One. Śākalya said: Om.
Śākalya asked: Which are those three and three hundred, three and three thousand? ॥3.9.1॥
3.9.2: Yājñavalkya said: These are only their glories (mahiman); the gods are only thirty-three. Śākalya asked: Which are those thirty-three? Yājñavalkya said: The eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras, the twelve Ādityas: these make thirty-one; and Indra and Prajāpati make up the thirty-three. ॥3.9.2॥
3.9.3: Śākalya asked: Which are the Vasus? Yājñavalkya said: Fire and earth, air and the mid-region, the sun and heaven, the moon and the stars: they are the Vasus, since in them all this is placed to dwell (vasu); therefore they are the Vasus. ॥3.9.3॥
3.9.4: Śākalya asked: Which are the Rudras?

Yājñavalkya said: These ten prāṇas (the organs) in a man, the eleventh being the self (ātman). When they go out of this mortal body, they make (his kin) weep; because they make them weep, they are the Rudras. ॥3.9.4॥
3.9.5: Śākalya asked: Which are the Ādityas?
Yājñavalkya said: The twelve months of the year are the Ādityas, for they move on, taking up all this; because they move on taking up (ādadānāḥ) all this, they are the Ādityas. ॥3.9.5॥
3.9.6: Śākalya asked: Which is Indra, which is Prajāpati?
Yājñavalkya said: The thunder (stanayitnu) is Indra, the sacrifice is Prajāpati.
Śākalya asked: Which is the thunder? Yājñavalkya said: The thunderbolt (aśani).
Śākalya asked: Which is the sacrifice?
3.9.7: Śākalya asked: Which are the six? Yājñavalkya said: Fire and earth, air and the mid-region, the sun and heaven: these are the six, for all this is these six. ॥3.9.7॥
3.9.8: Śākalya asked: Which are the three gods? Yājñavalkya said: These three worlds, for all these gods are in them.
Śākalya asked: Which are the two gods? Yājñavalkya said: Food and prāṇa, the vital breath.
Śākalya asked: Which is the one and a half?
Yājñavalkya said: He who blows here (the wind). ॥3.9.8॥
3.9.9: On this they say: he blows as though he were one only;
how, then, is he one and a half?
Because in him all this grew to greatness (adhyārdhnot), therefore he is the one and a half (adhyardha).
Śākalya asked: Which is the one god?
Yājñavalkya said: Prāṇa. He is Brahman; they call him the beyond (tyat). ॥3.9.9॥
3.9.10: Śākalya said: The person whose abode is the earth alone, whose loka (means of seeing) is fire, whose light is the mind, the final support of the whole self: he who knows that person would indeed be a knower, Yājñavalkya.
Yājñavalkya said: I do know that person, the final support of the whole self, of whom you speak: it is this very person who dwells in the body (śārīra).
Ask on, Śākalya. Śākalya asked: Who is his deity? Yājñavalkya said: The immortal (amṛta). ॥3.9.10॥
3.9.11: Śākalya said: The person whose abode is desire alone, whose loka is the heart, whose light is the mind, the final support of the whole self: he who knows that person would indeed be a knower, Yājñavalkya.
Yājñavalkya said: I do know that person, the final support of the whole self, of whom you speak: it is this very person made of desire. Ask on, Śākalya. Śākalya asked: Who is his deity?
3.9.12: Śākalya said: The person whose abode is forms alone, whose loka is the eye, whose light is the mind, the final support of the whole self: he who knows that person would indeed be a knower, Yājñavalkya.
Yājñavalkya said: I do know that person, the final support of the whole self, of whom you speak: it is that very person in the sun. Ask on, Śākalya. Śākalya asked: Who is his deity?
3.9.13: Śākalya said: The person whose abode is space alone, whose loka is the ear, whose light is the mind, the final support of the whole self: he who knows that person would indeed be a knower, Yājñavalkya.

Yājñavalkya said: I do know that person, the final support of the whole self, of whom you speak: it is this very person who is in the ear and present at each hearing (prātiśrutka). Ask on, Śākalya. Śākalya asked: Who is his deity?
3.9.14: Śākalya said: The person whose abode is darkness alone, whose loka is the heart, whose light is the mind, the final support of the whole self: he who knows that person would indeed be a knower, Yājñavalkya.
Yājñavalkya said: I do know that person, the final support of the whole self, of whom you speak: it is this very person made of shadow. Ask on, Śākalya. Śākalya asked: Who is his deity?
3.9.15: Śākalya said: The person whose abode is forms alone, whose loka is the eye, whose light is the mind, the final support of the whole self: he who knows that person would indeed be a knower, Yājñavalkya.

Yājñavalkya said: I do know that person, the final support of the whole self, of whom you speak: it is this very person in the mirror. Ask on, Śākalya. Śākalya asked: Who is his deity? Yājñavalkya said: Life (asu). ॥3.9.15॥
3.9.16: Śākalya said: The person whose abode is the waters alone, whose loka is the heart, whose light is the mind, the final support of the whole self: he who knows that person would indeed be a knower, Yājñavalkya.
Yājñavalkya said: I do know that person, the final support of the whole self, of whom you speak: it is this very person in the waters. Ask on, Śākalya. Śākalya asked: Who is his deity?
3.9.17: Śākalya said: The person whose abode is semen alone, whose loka is the heart, whose light is the mind, the final support of the whole self: he who knows that person would indeed be a knower, Yājñavalkya.
Yājñavalkya said: I do know that person, the final support of the whole self, of whom you speak: it is this very person made of the son. Ask on, Śākalya. Śākalya asked: Who is his deity?
3.9.18: Yājñavalkya said: Śākalya, have these brāhmaṇas, I wonder, made you their tongs for the burning coals? ॥3.9.18॥
3.9.19: Śākalya said: Yājñavalkya, you have belittled the brāhmaṇas of the Kurus and the Pañcālas: what Brahman do you know, that you do so?
Yājñavalkya said: I know the quarters with their gods and their supports.
Śākalya said: If you know the quarters with their gods and their supports, ॥3.9.19॥
3.9.20: What is your deity in this eastern quarter? Yājñavalkya said: The sun (Āditya) is my deity.
Śākalya asked: In what is that sun supported?
Śākalya asked: And in what is the eye supported?
Yājñavalkya said: In forms, for it is with the eye that one sees forms.
Śākalya asked: And in what are forms supported?
Yājñavalkya said: In the heart, for it is with the heart that one knows forms; in the heart alone are forms supported. Śākalya said: Just so, Yājñavalkya. ॥3.9.20॥
3.9.21: Śākalya asked: What is your deity in this southern quarter?
Yājñavalkya said: Yama is my deity.
Śākalya asked: In what is that Yama supported?
Śākalya asked: And in what is the sacrifice supported?
Yājñavalkya said: In the priests' fee (dakṣiṇā).

Śākalya asked: And in what is the fee supported? Yājñavalkya said: In faith (śraddhā), for only when a man has faith does he give the fee; in faith alone is the fee supported. Śākalya asked: And in what is faith supported? Yājñavalkya said: In the heart, for it is with the heart that one knows faith; in the heart alone is faith supported. Śākalya said: Just so, Yājñavalkya. ॥3.9.21॥
3.9.22: Śākalya asked: What is your deity in this western quarter?
Yājñavalkya said: Varuṇa is my deity.
Śākalya asked: In what is that Varuṇa supported? Yājñavalkya said: In the waters.
Śākalya asked: And in what are the waters supported? Yājñavalkya said: In semen.

Śākalya asked: And in what is semen supported? Yājñavalkya said: In the heart. That is why, of a son born in his father's likeness, people say: He has, as it were, slipped out of his heart; he is, as it were, made from his heart; for in the heart alone is semen supported. Śākalya said: Just so, Yājñavalkya. ॥3.9.22॥
3.9.23: Śākalya asked: What is your deity in this northern quarter?
Yājñavalkya said: Soma is my deity.
Śākalya asked: In what is that Soma supported?

Śākalya asked: And in what is the consecration supported? Yājñavalkya said: In truth. That is why they say to one who has been consecrated: Speak the truth; for in truth alone is the consecration supported. Śākalya asked: And in what is truth supported? Yājñavalkya said: In the heart, for it is with the heart that one knows truth; in the heart alone is truth supported. Śākalya said: Just so, Yājñavalkya. ॥3.9.23॥
3.9.24: Śākalya asked: What is your deity in this fixed quarter (dhruvā)? Yājñavalkya said: Agni, fire, is my deity.
Śākalya asked: In what is that Agni supported? Yājñavalkya said: In speech.
Śākalya asked: And in what is speech supported? Yājñavalkya said: In the heart.
Śākalya asked: And in what is the heart supported? ॥3.9.24॥
3.9.25: Yājñavalkya said: Ahallika, when you think that this (heart) is somewhere other than in us,
for if it were somewhere other than in us, dogs would eat it (the body) or birds would tear it apart. ॥3.9.25॥
3.9.26: Śākalya asked: In what are you (the body) and your self supported?
Śākalya asked: And in what is prāṇa supported? Yājñavalkya said: In apāna.
Śākalya asked: And in what is apāna supported?
Śākalya asked: And in what is vyāna supported? Yājñavalkya said: In udāna.
Śākalya asked: And in what is udāna supported?

This Self is the one spoken of as not thus, not thus (neti neti). He is ungraspable, for he is not grasped; undecaying, for he does not decay; unattached, for he does not cling; he is unbound, he does not suffer, he is not hurt. These are the eight abodes, the eight lokas, the eight deities, the eight persons.
He who set out those persons apart, drew them back and passed beyond them: about that person taught in the Upaniṣads (aupaniṣada) I ask you.
If you do not explain him to me, your head will fall off.
Śākalya did not know him, and his head fell off; and robbers carried away even his bones, taking them for something else. ॥3.9.26॥
3.9.27: Then Yājñavalkya said: Revered brāhmaṇas, let whoever of you wishes question me, or let all of you question me; or whoever of you wishes, I will question him, or I will question all of you.
3.9.28: Yājñavalkya questioned them with these verses: As a tree, the lord of the forest, so truly is a man: his hairs are its leaves, his skin its outer bark.
From his skin his blood flows out, from its bark its sap; so from him, when he is wounded, it comes forth as sap does from a tree that is struck.
His flesh is its pieces of wood (śakara), his sinews its inner bark (kināṭa), which is firm.
His bones within are its wood; his marrow is made like its marrow.
If a tree, when it is cut down, grows again from its root, newer than before, from what root, then, does a mortal grow when death has cut him down?
Do not say: From semen; for that is produced from the living. A tree springs also from the seed, and when it has died it comes into being again directly.
If they were to tear the tree out with its root, it would not come into being again.
From what root, then, does a mortal grow when death has cut him down?

If you say he is born already: no, he is born again; who, then, would bring him forth again? Brahman is consciousness and bliss, the final goal of the giver of wealth, and of him who stands firm in it and knows it. ॥3.9.28॥
4.1.1: Om. Janaka Vaideha was seated, giving audience. Then Yājñavalkya came to him.
Janaka said to him: Yājñavalkya, for what purpose have you come: wanting cattle, or subtle questions (aṇvanta)? Yājñavalkya said: Both, O emperor. ॥4.1.1॥
4.1.2: Yājñavalkya said: Let us hear whatever anyone has told you. Janaka said: Jitvan Śailini told me: Speech is Brahman.

Yājñavalkya said: As one taught by a mother, a father and a teacher would say it, so Śailini said that speech is Brahman, for what could one have who does not speak? But did he tell you its abode and its support?
Janaka said: He did not tell me. Yājñavalkya said: Then this (Brahman) has only one foot, O emperor.
Janaka said: Then you tell us, Yājñavalkya.
Yājñavalkya said: Speech itself is its abode, space its support; one should worship it as intelligence (prajñā).
Janaka asked: What is its intelligence, Yājñavalkya?

Yājñavalkya said: Speech itself, O emperor. It is by speech, O emperor, that a kinsman is known; the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, the Atharvāṅgirasa, the itihāsas, the purāṇas, the sciences (vidyā), the Upaniṣads, the verses (ślokas), the aphorisms (sūtras), the glosses (anuvyākhyānas) and the commentaries (vyākhyānas), what is sacrificed, what is offered in the fire, what is given to eat and what is given to drink, this world and the other world, and all beings are known by speech alone, O emperor. Speech, O emperor, is the highest Brahman. Speech does not leave him; all beings flow towards him (with offerings).
He who, knowing thus, worships it becomes a god and goes to the gods.
Janaka Vaideha said: I give a thousand cows with an elephant-like bull.
Yājñavalkya said: My father held that one should not take (wealth from a pupil) without having fully instructed him. ॥4.1.2॥
4.1.3: Yājñavalkya said: Let us hear whatever anyone has told you. Janaka said: Udaṅka Śaulbāyana told me: Prāṇa, the vital breath, is Brahman.

Yājñavalkya said: As one taught by a mother, a father and a teacher would say it, so Śaulbāyana said that prāṇa is Brahman, for what could one have who does not breathe? But did he tell you its abode and its support?
Janaka said: He did not tell me. Yājñavalkya said: Then this (Brahman) has only one foot, O emperor.
Janaka said: Then you tell us, Yājñavalkya.
Yājñavalkya said: Prāṇa itself is its abode, space its support; one should worship it as the dear (priya).
Janaka asked: What is its dearness, Yājñavalkya?

Yājñavalkya said: Prāṇa itself, O emperor. For the sake of prāṇa, O emperor, a man officiates at the sacrifice of one for whom he should not, and accepts gifts from one from whom he should not; and in whatever quarter he goes, there is fear of being killed: all for the sake of prāṇa, O emperor. Prāṇa, O emperor, is the highest Brahman.
Prāṇa does not leave him; all beings flow towards him.
He who, knowing thus, worships it becomes a god and goes to the gods.
Janaka Vaideha said: I give a thousand cows with an elephant-like bull.
Yājñavalkya said: My father held that one should not take (wealth from a pupil) without having fully instructed him. ॥4.1.3॥
4.1.4: Yājñavalkya said: Let us hear whatever anyone has told you. Janaka said: Barku Vārṣṇa told me: The eye is Brahman.

Yājñavalkya said: As one taught by a mother, a father and a teacher would say it, so Vārṣṇa said that the eye is Brahman, for what could one have who does not see? But did he tell you its abode and its support?
Janaka said: He did not tell me. Yājñavalkya said: Then this (Brahman) has only one foot, O emperor.
Janaka said: Then you tell us, Yājñavalkya.
Yājñavalkya said: The eye itself is its abode, space its support; one should worship it as truth (satya).
Janaka asked: What is its truth, Yājñavalkya?
Yājñavalkya said: The eye itself, O emperor. To one who sees with his eye, O emperor, people say: Did you see?
He says: I saw; and that is truth. The eye, O emperor, is the highest Brahman. The eye does not leave him; all beings flow towards him.
He who, knowing thus, worships it becomes a god and goes to the gods.
Janaka Vaideha said: I give a thousand cows with an elephant-like bull.
Yājñavalkya said: My father held that one should not take (wealth from a pupil) without having fully instructed him. ॥4.1.4॥
4.1.5: Yājñavalkya said: Let us hear whatever anyone has told you. Janaka said: Gardabhīvipīta Bhāradvāja told me: The ear is Brahman. Yājñavalkya said: As one taught by a mother, a father and a teacher would say it, so Bhāradvāja said that the ear is Brahman, for what could one have who does not hear? But did he tell you its abode and its support?
Janaka said: He did not tell me. Yājñavalkya said: Then this (Brahman) has only one foot, O emperor.
Janaka said: Then you tell us, Yājñavalkya.
Yājñavalkya said: The ear itself is its abode, space its support; one should worship it as the endless (ananta).
Janaka asked: What is its endlessness, Yājñavalkya?

Yājñavalkya said: The quarters themselves, O emperor. That is why, O emperor, to whatever quarter a man goes, he never reaches its end, for the quarters are endless. The quarters, O emperor, are the ear; the ear in turn, O emperor, is the highest Brahman.
The ear does not leave him; all beings flow towards him.
He who, knowing thus, worships it becomes a god and goes to the gods.
Janaka Vaideha said: I give a thousand cows with an elephant-like bull.
Yājñavalkya said: My father held that one should not take (wealth from a pupil) without having fully instructed him. ॥4.1.5॥
4.1.6: Yājñavalkya said: Let us hear whatever anyone has told you. Janaka said: Satyakāma Jābāla told me: The mind is Brahman. Yājñavalkya said: As one taught by a mother, a father and a teacher would say it, so Jābāla said that the mind is Brahman, for what could one have who has no mind? But did he tell you its abode and its support?
Janaka said: He did not tell me. Yājñavalkya said: Then this (Brahman) has only one foot, O emperor.
Janaka said: Then you tell us, Yājñavalkya.
Yājñavalkya said: The mind itself is its abode, space its support; one should worship it as bliss (ānanda).
Janaka asked: What is its bliss, Yājñavalkya?
Yājñavalkya said: The mind itself, O emperor. It is by the mind, O emperor, that a man is drawn to a woman; a son like him is born of her; he is bliss.
The mind, O emperor, is the highest Brahman. The mind does not leave him; all beings flow towards him.
He who, knowing thus, worships it becomes a god and goes to the gods.
Janaka Vaideha said: I give a thousand cows with an elephant-like bull.
Yājñavalkya said: My father held that one should not take (wealth from a pupil) without having fully instructed him. ॥4.1.6॥
4.1.7: Yājñavalkya said: Let us hear whatever anyone has told you. Janaka said: Vidagdha Śākalya told me: The heart is Brahman. Yājñavalkya said: As one taught by a mother, a father and a teacher would say it, so Śākalya said that the heart is Brahman, for what could one have who has no heart? But did he tell you its abode and its support?
Janaka said: He did not tell me. Yājñavalkya said: Then this (Brahman) has only one foot, O emperor.
Janaka said: Then you tell us, Yājñavalkya.
Yājñavalkya said: The heart itself is its abode, space its support; one should worship it as stability (sthiti).
Janaka asked: What is its stability, Yājñavalkya?

Yājñavalkya said: The heart itself, O emperor. The heart, O emperor, is all beings' abode; the heart, O emperor, is all beings' support, for in the heart alone, O emperor, all beings are supported. The heart, O emperor, is the highest Brahman. The heart does not leave him; all beings flow towards him.
He who, knowing thus, worships it becomes a god and goes to the gods.
Janaka Vaideha said: I give a thousand cows with an elephant-like bull.
Yājñavalkya said: My father held that one should not take (wealth from a pupil) without having fully instructed him. ॥4.1.7॥
4.2.1: Janaka Vaideha came down from his seat (kūrca), approached him and said: Salutation to you, Yājñavalkya; instruct me.

Yājñavalkya said: As a man about to go on a long journey, O emperor, would take a chariot or a boat, so your mind is well furnished with these secret names (upaniṣads); being thus eminent and wealthy, having studied the Vedas and been taught the upaniṣads, where will you go when you are released from here?
Janaka said: I do not know, revered sir, where I shall go. Yājñavalkya said: Then I will tell you where you will go.
Janaka said: Let the revered one tell me. ॥4.2.1॥
4.2.2: Yājñavalkya said: This person who is in the right eye is named Indha; him, who is Indha, they call Indra, indirectly, for the gods are fond, as it were, of the indirect and dislike the direct. ॥4.2.2॥
4.2.3: Now this form of a person in the left eye is his wife, Virāj. Their meeting place (saṃstāva) is the space within the heart; their food is the red lump within the heart; their covering is the network, as it were, within the heart; and their path for going about is the channel (nāḍī) that rises upward from the heart.

Like a hair split a thousandfold are these channels of his, called hitā, which are set within the heart; through them this (essence of food) flows on; therefore this one (the subtle self) is, as it were, a feeder on finer food than the bodily self. ॥4.2.3॥
4.2.4: For him the eastern quarter is the eastward prāṇas, the vital breaths; the southern quarter the southward prāṇas; the western quarter the westward prāṇas; the northern quarter the northward prāṇas; the upper quarter the upward prāṇas; the lower quarter the downward prāṇas; all the quarters all the prāṇas.

This Self is the one spoken of as not thus, not thus (neti neti). He is ungraspable, for he is not grasped; undecaying, for he does not decay; unattached, for he does not cling; he is unbound, he does not suffer, he is not hurt. Yājñavalkya said: Janaka, you have reached freedom from fear (abhaya).
Janaka Vaideha said: May freedom from fear come to you too, Yājñavalkya, revered sir, you who make us know freedom from fear. Salutation to you. Here are the Videhas, and here I am. ॥4.2.4॥
4.3.1: Yājñavalkya went to Janaka Vaideha, thinking: I will not speak. But once, when Janaka Vaideha and Yājñavalkya had talked together about the Agnihotra, the daily fire offering, Yājñavalkya had given him a boon.
Janaka had chosen the boon of asking questions as he wished.
Yājñavalkya had granted it to him.
So it was the emperor who questioned him first. ॥4.3.1॥
4.3.2: Janaka asked: Yājñavalkya, what light does this person have? Yājñavalkya said: He has the sun for his light, O emperor; it is by the sun as his light that he sits, goes about, does his work and comes back. Janaka said: It is just so, Yājñavalkya. ॥4.3.2॥
4.3.3: Janaka asked: When the sun has set, Yājñavalkya, what light does this person have?
Yājñavalkya said: The moon is his light; it is by the moon as his light that he sits, goes about, does his work and comes back. Janaka said: It is just so, Yājñavalkya. ॥4.3.3॥
4.3.4: Janaka asked: When the sun has set, Yājñavalkya, and the moon has set, what light does this person have? Yājñavalkya said: Fire is his light; it is by fire as his light that he sits, goes about, does his work and comes back. Janaka said: It is just so, Yājñavalkya. ॥4.3.4॥
4.3.5: Janaka asked: When the sun has set, Yājñavalkya, and the moon has set, and the fire has gone out, what light does this person have?
Yājñavalkya said: Speech is his light; it is by speech as his light that he sits, goes about, does his work and comes back.
That is why, O emperor, even where one cannot make out one's own hand, one goes straight to the place where a voice is raised. Janaka said: It is just so, Yājñavalkya. ॥4.3.5॥
4.3.6: Janaka asked: When the sun has set, Yājñavalkya, and the moon has set, and the fire has gone out, and speech has fallen silent, what light does this person have? Yājñavalkya said: The self (ātman) is his light; it is by the self as his light that he sits, goes about, does his work and comes back. ॥4.3.6॥
4.3.7: Janaka asked: Which is the self?
Yājñavalkya said: It is this person, made of knowledge (vijñānamaya) among the prāṇas (the organs), the light within the heart. Being like (the intellect), he moves through both worlds.
He seems to meditate, he seems to move about; for, having become dream, he passes beyond this world, beyond the forms of death. ॥4.3.7॥
4.3.8: This person, when he is born and takes on a body, is joined with evils (pāpman).
When he departs, dying, he leaves the evils behind. ॥4.3.8॥
4.3.9: This person has just two states: this one and the state of the other world. The third, the state of dream, is the junction between them; standing in that junction, he sees both these states, this one and the state of the other world. Whatever footing (ākrama) he has towards the state of the other world, taking that footing he sees both evils and joys. When he falls asleep, he takes a portion (mātrā) of this all-holding world, himself lays (the body) low, himself builds (a dream body), and sleeps by his own radiance, by his own light. Here this person is his own light. ॥4.3.9॥
4.3.10: There are no chariots there, no teams to draw them, no roads; but he makes chariots, teams and roads.
There are no joys there, no delights, no great delights; but he makes joys, delights and great delights.
There are no ponds there, no pools, no rivers; but he makes ponds, pools and rivers, for he is the maker. ॥4.3.10॥
4.3.11: On this there are these verses: Striking down the body through dream, himself not sleeping, he looks upon the sleeping (all things, present only as impressions).
Taking the bright (light of the senses), he comes back again to his place: the golden person, the lone swan. ॥4.3.11॥
4.3.12: Guarding his lowly nest (the body) by prāṇa, the vital breath, the immortal one roams outside the nest; immortal, he goes wherever he wishes: the golden person, the lone swan. ॥4.3.12॥
4.3.13: In dream, going to high and low states, the shining one (deva) makes many forms.
Now he seems to delight with women and to laugh, now he seems to see fearful things. ॥4.3.13॥
4.3.14: All see his play; no one sees him.
They say: One should not wake him suddenly.
If this (self) does not find its way back to its place, the body becomes hard to cure.
And some say: This (dream) is only his waking state, for the things he sees awake are the very things he sees asleep. Yet here this person is his own light.
Janaka said: I give you, revered sir, a thousand (cows). Speak further, for my freedom. ॥4.3.14॥
4.3.15: Yājñavalkya said: Having enjoyed himself and roamed in this deep sleep (samprasāda), and having only seen good and evil, he comes back again the way he came, to his place, to dream. Whatever he sees there does not follow him, for this person is unattached. Janaka said: It is just so, Yājñavalkya.
I give you, revered sir, a thousand (cows). Speak further, for my freedom. ॥4.3.15॥
4.3.16: Yājñavalkya said: Having enjoyed himself and roamed in this dream, and having only seen good and evil, he comes back again the way he came, to his place, to waking. Whatever he sees there does not follow him, for this person is unattached. Janaka said: It is just so, Yājñavalkya.
I give you, revered sir, a thousand (cows). Speak further, for my freedom. ॥4.3.16॥
4.3.17: Yājñavalkya said: Having enjoyed himself and roamed in this waking state, and having only seen good and evil, he comes back again the way he came, to his place, to the state of dream (svapnānta). ॥4.3.17॥
4.3.18: As a great fish moves by turns along both banks, the near and the far, so this person moves by turns through both these states, the state of dream and the state of waking. ॥4.3.18॥
4.3.19: As a falcon or an eagle (suparṇa), having flown about in this sky, grows weary, folds its wings and bears itself down to its nest, so this person hastens to that state where, asleep, he desires no desire and sees no dream. ॥4.3.19॥
4.3.20: These are his channels called hitā, as fine as a hair split a thousandfold, and they are full of white, blue, tawny, green and red (fluid). Now when it seems that they are killing him, that they are overpowering him, that an elephant is chasing him, that he is falling into a pit, then whatever fearful thing he sees when awake he imagines here through ignorance. And when he thinks himself a god, as it were, a king, as it were, and when he thinks: I alone am all this, that is his highest world. ॥4.3.20॥
4.3.21: That indeed is his form beyond desires, free from evils, without fear.

As a man in the embrace of a beloved woman knows nothing without and nothing within, so this person, in the embrace of the knowing Self (prājña), knows nothing without and nothing within. That indeed is his form in which desires are fulfilled, in which the Self is the desire, which is without desire and beyond sorrow. ॥4.3.21॥
4.3.22: Here a father is no father, a mother no mother, the worlds are not worlds, the gods are not gods, the Vedas are not Vedas. Here a thief is no thief, the killer of an embryo no killer of an embryo, a Cāṇḍāla no Cāṇḍāla, a Paulkasa no Paulkasa, a monk (śramaṇa) no monk, an ascetic (tāpasa) no ascetic. (This form) is untouched by good, untouched by evil, for then he has passed beyond all the sorrows of the heart. ॥4.3.22॥
4.3.23: When there he does not see, he is in truth seeing, though he does not see; for the seeing of the seer is never lost, since it is imperishable. But no second exists then, other than him and separate from him, that he could see. ॥4.3.23॥
4.3.24: When there he does not smell, he is in truth smelling, though he does not smell; for the smelling of the smeller is never lost, since it is imperishable. But no second exists then, other than him and separate from him, that he could smell. ॥4.3.24॥
4.3.25: When there he does not taste, he is in truth tasting, though he does not taste; for the tasting of the taster is never lost, since it is imperishable. But no second exists then, other than him and separate from him, that he could taste. ॥4.3.25॥
4.3.26: When there he does not speak, he is in truth speaking, though he does not speak; for the speaking of the speaker is never lost, since it is imperishable. But no second exists then, other than him and separate from him, that he could speak. ॥4.3.26॥
4.3.27: When there he does not hear, he is in truth hearing, though he does not hear; for the hearing of the hearer is never lost, since it is imperishable. But no second exists then, other than him and separate from him, that he could hear. ॥4.3.27॥
4.3.28: When there he does not think, he is in truth thinking, though he does not think; for the thinking of the thinker is never lost, since it is imperishable. But no second exists then, other than him and separate from him, that he could think of. ॥4.3.28॥
4.3.29: When there he does not touch, he is in truth touching, though he does not touch; for the touching of the toucher is never lost, since it is imperishable. But no second exists then, other than him and separate from him, that he could touch. ॥4.3.29॥
4.3.30: When there he does not know, he is in truth knowing, though he does not know; for the knowing of the knower is never lost, since it is imperishable. But no second exists then, other than him and separate from him, that he could know. ॥4.3.30॥
4.3.31: Where there is, as it were, another, there one may see another, one may smell another, one may taste another, one may speak to another, one may hear another, one may think of another, one may touch another, one may know another. ॥4.3.31॥
4.3.32: He becomes (clear) as water, one, the seer, without a second. This is the world of Brahman, O emperor: thus Yājñavalkya taught him.
This is his highest goal, this his highest treasure, this his highest world, this his highest bliss. Other beings live on a portion of this very bliss. ॥4.3.32॥
4.3.33: He who among men is whole of body and prosperous, a lord over others, most richly endowed with all human enjoyments: he is the highest bliss of men. A hundred blisses of men are one bliss of the fathers who have won their world. A hundred blisses of the fathers who have won their world are one bliss in the world of the gandharvas. A hundred blisses in the world of the gandharvas are one bliss of the gods by works, who reach godhood by their works. A hundred blisses of the gods by works are one bliss of the gods by birth, and of him who is learned in the Veda (śrotriya), sinless and not struck by desire. A hundred blisses of the gods by birth are one bliss in the world of Prajāpati, and of him who is learned in the Veda, sinless and not struck by desire. A hundred blisses in the world of Prajāpati are one bliss in the world of Brahmā, and of him who is learned in the Veda, sinless and not struck by desire. And this is the highest bliss. This is the world of Brahman, O emperor, said Yājñavalkya.
Janaka said: I give you, revered sir, a thousand (cows). Speak further, for my freedom. At this Yājñavalkya grew afraid: The king is intelligent; he has hemmed me in at all my conclusions. ॥4.3.33॥
4.3.34: Yājñavalkya said: Having enjoyed himself and roamed in this state of dream (svapnānta), and having only seen good and evil, he comes back again the way he came, to his place, to waking. ॥4.3.34॥
4.3.35: As a heavily laden cart goes creaking, just so this embodied self, mounted by the knowing Self (prājña), goes groaning, when he comes to breathe upward. ॥4.3.35॥
4.3.36: When this (body) grows thin — it grows thin through old age or through illness — then, as a mango or a fig (udumbara) or a pippala fruit comes loose from its stalk, just so this person, freeing himself wholly from these limbs, hastens back again the way he came, to a (new) birth, for prāṇa alone. ॥4.3.36॥
4.3.37: As, for a king who is coming, the Ugras, the officers who punish offenders (pratyenas), the Sūtas and the village heads wait ready with food, drink and lodgings, saying: Here he comes, here he arrives; just so, for one who knows thus, all beings wait ready, saying: Here comes Brahman, here it arrives. ॥4.3.37॥
4.3.38: As, when a king is about to set out, the Ugras, the officers who punish offenders, the Sūtas and the village heads gather round him, just so at the time of death all the prāṇas (the organs) gather round this self, when he comes to breathe upward. ॥4.3.38॥
4.4.1: When this self comes to weakness and comes, as it were, to bewilderment, then these prāṇas (the organs) gather round him. Drawing these particles of light (tejomātrā) wholly into himself, it is into the heart that he comes down. When the person in the eye turns away and goes back, then he no longer knows forms. ॥4.4.1॥
4.4.2: (The organ) becomes one (with him); he does not see, they say. It becomes one; he does not smell, they say. It becomes one; he does not taste, they say. It becomes one; he does not speak, they say. It becomes one; he does not hear, they say. It becomes one; he does not think, they say. It becomes one; he does not touch, they say. It becomes one; he does not know, they say. Then the tip of his heart lights up, and by that light this self goes out, through the eye, or through the head, or through other parts of the body. As he goes out, prāṇa, the vital breath, goes out after him; as prāṇa goes out, all the prāṇas (the organs) go out after it.
He comes to have particular awareness, and it is into what has awareness that he passes.
Knowledge and work take hold of him and follow him, and so does his past experience (pūrvaprajñā). ॥4.4.2॥
4.4.3: As a leech on a blade of grass, coming to the end of the blade, takes hold of another support and draws itself over onto it, just so this self, casting down this body and making it unconscious, takes hold of another support and draws itself over onto it. ॥4.4.3॥
4.4.4: As a goldsmith, taking a piece of gold, fashions another form, newer and more beautiful, just so this self, casting down this body and making it unconscious, makes for itself another form, newer and more beautiful: that of the fathers, or of the gandharvas, or of the gods, or of Prajāpati, or of Brahmā, or of other beings. ॥4.4.4॥
4.4.5: This Self is indeed Brahman: made of knowledge (vijñāna), made of mind, made of prāṇa, made of the eye, made of the ear, made of earth, made of water, made of air, made of space, made of light and of what is not light, made of desire and of desirelessness, made of anger and of freedom from anger, made of dharma (right conduct) and of adharma, made of everything. This is what is meant by: he is made of this, made of that. As he acts, as he conducts himself, so he becomes.
The doer of good becomes good, the doer of evil becomes evil. One becomes virtuous by virtuous work, sinful by sinful work.

And some indeed say: This person is made of desire alone. As his desire is, so is his resolve (kratu); as his resolve is, so is the work he does; whatever work he does, that (its fruit) he attains. ॥4.4.5॥
4.4.6: On this there is a verse:
Attached, he goes with his karma, his deeds, to that very thing on which his mind, the liṅga, is set.
When he has come to the end of (the fruit of) whatever work he does here,

he comes back again from that world to this world, for work. So it is with the man who desires. Now the man who does not desire: he who is without desire, freed from desire, whose desires are fulfilled, whose desire is the Self — his prāṇas do not go out; being none other than Brahman, he goes to Brahman. ॥4.4.6॥
4.4.7: On this there is a verse: When all the desires lodged in his heart are let go,
then the mortal becomes immortal; here (in this body) he attains Brahman.

And just as a snake's slough lies on an anthill, dead and cast off, so this body lies. But this bodiless, immortal prāṇa is Brahman alone, is light alone. Janaka Vaideha said: I give you, revered sir, a thousand (cows). ॥4.4.7॥
4.4.8: On this there are these verses:
The subtle path, wide and ancient, has reached me; I myself have found it in full.
By it the wise, the knowers of Brahman, go from here upward, freed, to the heavenly world. ॥4.4.8॥
4.4.9: In it, they say, there is white, or blue, tawny, green and red.
This path was found by the brāhmaṇa; by it goes the knower of Brahman who has done good and is full of light (taijasa). ॥4.4.9॥
4.4.10: Those who worship avidyā enter blind darkness;
into darkness greater still, as it were, go those who delight in vidyā. ॥4.4.10॥
4.4.11: Those worlds are called “joyless”, covered in blind darkness. People who are unlearned and unawakened go to them after death. ॥4.4.11॥
4.4.12: If a person should know the Self as: I am this — then wishing for what, and for whose desire, would he follow the body in its suffering? ॥4.4.12॥
4.4.13: He who has found and awakened to the Self that has entered this deep, impenetrable body
is the maker of all, for he is the doer of everything; the world is his, and he indeed is the world itself. ॥4.4.13॥
4.4.14: While we are still here, we have come to know it; had we not, I would have remained ignorant, and great would have been the destruction.
Those who know it become immortal; but the others go only to sorrow. ॥4.4.14॥
4.4.15: When one directly beholds this Self, the shining one (deva),
the lord of the past and the future, he no longer seeks to hide himself from him. ॥4.4.15॥
4.4.16: That on this side of which the year revolves with its days,
that light of lights, the immortal, the gods worship as life. ॥4.4.16॥
4.4.17: That in which the five pañcajanas (the five kinds of beings) and space are established,
that alone I regard as the Self, the immortal Brahman; knowing it, I am immortal. ॥4.4.17॥
4.4.18: Those who know the prāṇa of the prāṇa and the eye of the eye and the ear of the ear, and who know the mind of the mind,
have known for certain the ancient, primordial Brahman. ॥4.4.18॥
4.4.19: By the (purified) mind alone is this to be seen; there is no difference here at all.
He who sees as if there were difference here goes from death to death. ॥4.4.19॥
4.4.20: In one way alone is this to be seen, this immeasurable, unchanging one.
The Self is stainless, beyond space, unborn, great, imperishable. ॥4.4.20॥
4.4.21: Knowing him alone, the wise brāhmaṇa should gain insight (prajñā);
he should not dwell on many words, for that is a wearying of speech. ॥4.4.21॥
4.4.22: This great unborn Self is he who is made of knowledge (vijñānamaya) among the prāṇas (the organs).
