In the space that is within the heart he lies; he is the controller of all, the ruler of all, the sovereign of all. He does not become greater by good work, nor any less by bad work. He is the lord of all, the sovereign of beings, the protector of beings; he is the dam (setu) that holds these worlds apart, so that they do not run into one another.

Him the brāhmaṇas seek to know by Vedic study, by sacrifice, by gifts, and by austerity that is a fasting from desires (anāśaka). Knowing him alone one becomes a muni, a man of meditation. Desiring him alone as their world, renunciates go forth from home. It was for this that the knowers of old did not desire offspring, thinking: What shall we do with offspring, we whose world is this Self?

They rose above the desire for sons, the desire for wealth and the desire for worlds, and then went about begging alms. For the desire for sons is itself the desire for wealth, and the desire for wealth is itself the desire for worlds; both of these are only desires.

This Self is the one spoken of as not thus, not thus (neti neti). He is ungraspable, for he is not grasped; undecaying, for he does not decay; unattached, for he does not cling; he is unbound, he does not suffer, he is not hurt. These two do not overcome him, the thought For this I did evil and the thought For this I did good; he overcomes both of them. What he has done and what he has left undone do not burn him. ॥4.4.22॥
4.4.23: This has been declared by a ṛc, a verse of the Veda:
This is the eternal greatness of the brāhmaṇa (the knower of Brahman): it does not grow greater by work, nor does it become less.
One should know the very nature of that (greatness); knowing it, one is not stained by evil work.

Therefore he who knows thus, being calm, restrained, withdrawn, enduring and collected, sees the Self in himself; he sees all as the Self. No evil overcomes him; he overcomes all evil. No evil burns him; he burns all evil. He becomes a brāhmaṇa free from evil, free from passion (rajas), free from doubt. This is the world that is Brahman (brahmaloka), O emperor; you have been brought to it: so said Yājñavalkya.
Janaka said: I give you, revered sir, the Videhas, and myself too along with them, to be your servant. ॥4.4.23॥
4.4.24: This great unborn Self is the eater of food, the giver of wealth. He who knows thus finds wealth. ॥4.4.24॥
4.4.25: This great unborn Self is undecaying, undying, immortal, fearless; it is Brahman. Brahman indeed is fearless. He who knows thus surely becomes the fearless Brahman. ॥4.4.25॥
4.5.1: Now Yājñavalkya had two wives, Maitreyī and Kātyāyanī. Of the two, Maitreyī was one who discoursed on Brahman (brahmavādinī); Kātyāyanī at that time had only such understanding as women commonly had, concerned with the household. Then Yājñavalkya was about to take up another way of life (renunciation). ॥4.5.1॥
4.5.2: Yājñavalkya said: Maitreyī, my dear, I am about to go forth as a renunciate from this station (the householder's life).
Come, let me make a settlement between you and Kātyāyanī here (dividing what I have). ॥4.5.2॥
4.5.3: Maitreyī said: Revered sir, if this whole earth, filled with wealth, were mine, would I become immortal by it, or not? Yājñavalkya said: No. Your life would be just like the life of those who have plenty of means; but through wealth there is no hope of immortality. ॥4.5.3॥
4.5.4: Maitreyī said: What should I do with that which would not make me immortal?
Tell me just what you, revered sir, know (of the way to immortality). ॥4.5.4॥
4.5.5: Yājñavalkya said: You have indeed been dear to us, and now you have made what is dear grow greater. Come then, lady, I shall explain this to you; but while I explain, meditate deeply on what I say. ॥4.5.5॥
4.5.6: Yājñavalkya said: Not for the sake of the husband, my dear, is the husband dear; the husband is dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of the wife, my dear, is the wife dear; the wife is dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of sons, my dear, are sons dear; sons are dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of wealth, my dear, is wealth dear; wealth is dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of cattle, my dear, are cattle dear; cattle are dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of the priestly class (brahman), my dear, is the priestly class dear; the priestly class is dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of the ruling class (kṣatra), my dear, is the ruling class dear; the ruling class is dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of the worlds, my dear, are the worlds dear; the worlds are dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of the gods, my dear, are the gods dear; the gods are dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of the Vedas, my dear, are the Vedas dear; the Vedas are dear for the sake of the Self.
Not for the sake of beings, my dear, are beings dear; beings are dear for the sake of the Self.

Not for the sake of all, my dear, is all dear; all is dear for the sake of the Self. It is the Self, my dear, that is to be seen, to be heard, to be reflected on, to be meditated on. Maitreyī, my dear, when the Self indeed is seen, heard, reflected on and known, all this is known. ॥4.5.6॥
4.5.7: The priestly class rejects him who knows the priestly class as other than the Self; the ruling class rejects him who knows the ruling class as other than the Self; the worlds reject him who knows the worlds as other than the Self; the gods reject him who knows the gods as other than the Self; the Vedas reject him who knows the Vedas as other than the Self; beings reject him who knows beings as other than the Self; all rejects him who knows all as other than the Self. This priestly class, this ruling class, these worlds, these gods, these Vedas, these beings, all this, is what this Self is. ॥4.5.7॥
4.5.8: It is as with a drum being beaten: one cannot grasp its sounds as things outside it, but by grasping the drum, or the striking of the drum, the sound is grasped. ॥4.5.8॥
4.5.9: It is as with a conch being blown: one cannot grasp its sounds as things outside it, but by grasping the conch, or the one who blows the conch, the sound is grasped. ॥4.5.9॥
4.5.10: It is as with a vīṇā being played: one cannot grasp its sounds as things outside it, but by grasping the vīṇā, or the one who plays the vīṇā, the sound is grasped. ॥4.5.10॥
4.5.11: As from a fire laid with damp fuel clouds of smoke go forth in many ways, so, my dear, the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, the Atharvāṅgirasa (the Atharvaveda), the itihāsa (histories), the purāṇa (ancient lore), the vidyās (sciences), the Upaniṣads, the ślokas (verses), the sūtras (aphorisms), the anuvyākhyānas (explanations), the vyākhyānas (commentaries), sacrifice, oblation, food given, drink given, this world and the other world, and all beings are the breathing out of this great Being; all these are breathed out by this one alone. ॥4.5.11॥
4.5.12: As the ocean is the one place where all waters meet (ekāyana), so the skin is the one meeting place of all touches, the nose of all smells, the tongue of all tastes, the eye of all forms, the ear of all sounds, the mind of all resolves, the heart of all knowledge, the two hands of all actions, the organ of generation of all joys, the anus of all excretions, the two feet of all journeys, and speech of all the Vedas. ॥4.5.12॥
4.5.13: As a lump of salt is without inside or outside, entirely a mass of taste alone, so, my dear, this Self is without inside or outside, entirely a mass of consciousness (prajñāna) alone. Arising out of these elements, it vanishes along with them; after departing (from the body) there is no consciousness (saṃjñā). This is what I say, my dear: so said Yājñavalkya. ॥4.5.13॥
4.5.14: Maitreyī said: Just here, revered sir, you have brought me into the midst of bewilderment; I do not understand this (Self). Yājñavalkya said: I am not saying anything bewildering, my dear; this Self, my dear, is imperishable, by its nature never cut off. ॥4.5.14॥
4.5.15: For where there is duality, as it were, there one sees another, one smells another, one tastes another, one speaks to another, one hears another, one thinks of another, one touches another, one knows another.

But where everything has become the Self alone for him, then with what should one see whom, with what should one smell whom, with what should one taste whom, with what should one speak to whom, with what should one hear whom, with what should one think of whom, with what should one touch whom, with what should one know whom? By what should one know that by which one knows all this? This Self is the one spoken of as not thus, not thus (neti neti). He is ungraspable, for he is not grasped; undecaying, for he does not decay; unattached, for he does not cling; he is unbound, he does not suffer, he is not hurt.

By what, my dear, should one know the knower? You have now been given the teaching, Maitreyī; this much, my dear, is indeed immortality. Having said this, Yājñavalkya went away (into the wandering life). ॥4.5.15॥
4.6.1: Now the line of teachers. Pautimāṣya received this teaching from Gaupavana, Gaupavana from Pautimāṣya, Pautimāṣya from Gaupavana, Gaupavana from Kauśika, Kauśika from Kauṇḍinya, Kauṇḍinya from Śāṇḍilya, Śāṇḍilya from Kauśika and from Gautama, Gautama ॥4.6.1॥
4.6.2: from Āgniveśya, Āgniveśya from Gārgya, Gārgya from Gārgya, Gārgya from Gautama, Gautama from Saitava, Saitava from Pārāśaryāyaṇa, Pārāśaryāyaṇa from Gārgyāyaṇa, Gārgyāyaṇa from Uddālakāyana, Uddālakāyana from Jābālāyana, Jābālāyana from Mādhyandināyana, Mādhyandināyana from Saukarāyaṇa, Saukarāyaṇa from Kāṣāyaṇa, Kāṣāyaṇa from Sāyakāyana, Sāyakāyana from Kauśikāyani, Kauśikāyani ॥4.6.2॥
4.6.3: from Ghṛtakauśika, Ghṛtakauśika from Pārāśaryāyaṇa, Pārāśaryāyaṇa from Pārāśarya, Pārāśarya from Jātūkarṇya, Jātūkarṇya from Āsurāyaṇa and from Yāska, Āsurāyaṇa from Traivaṇi, Traivaṇi from Aupajandhani, Aupajandhani from Āsuri, Āsuri from Bhāradvāja, Bhāradvāja from Ātreya, Ātreya from Māṇṭi, Māṇṭi from Gautama, Gautama from Gautama, Gautama from Vātsya, Vātsya from Śāṇḍilya, Śāṇḍilya from Kaiśorya Kāpya, Kaiśorya Kāpya from Kumārahārita, Kumārahārita from Gālava, Gālava from Vidarbhīkauṇḍinya, Vidarbhīkauṇḍinya from Vatsanapāt Bābhrava, Vatsanapāt Bābhrava from Panthā Saubhara, Panthā Saubhara from Ayāsya Āṅgirasa, Ayāsya Āṅgirasa from Ābhūti Tvāṣṭra, Ābhūti Tvāṣṭra from Viśvarūpa Tvāṣṭra, Viśvarūpa Tvāṣṭra from the two Aśvins, the two Aśvins from Dadhyaṅ Ātharvaṇa, Dadhyaṅ Ātharvaṇa from Atharvan Daiva, Atharvan Daiva from Mṛtyu Prādhvaṃsana, Mṛtyu Prādhvaṃsana from Pradhvaṃsana, Pradhvaṃsana from Ekarṣi, Ekarṣi from Vipracitti, Vipracitti from Vyaṣṭi, Vyaṣṭi from Sanāru, Sanāru from Sanātana, Sanātana from Sanaga, Sanaga from Parameṣṭhin, Parameṣṭhin from Brahman. Brahman is self-existent. Salutation to Brahman. ॥4.6.3॥
5.1.1: Om. That (the unseen Brahman) is whole; this (the seen world) is whole. From the whole, the whole comes forth.
When the whole is taken from the whole, the whole alone remains.
Om is Brahman, space (kha). Space is the ancient one. Space is that which holds the air: so Kauravyāyaṇīputra used to say.
This (Om) is the Veda, so the brāhmaṇas know; for by it one knows what is to be known. ॥5.1.1॥
5.2.1: The three kinds of Prajāpati's offspring, the gods, men and demons (asuras), lived with their father Prajāpati as students, in brahmacarya. Having lived as students, the gods said: Speak to us, sir.
To them he spoke this syllable, da, and asked: Did you understand?
They said: We understood; you told us: Restrain yourselves (dāmyata). Prajāpati said: Yes (Om), you understood. ॥5.2.1॥
5.2.2: Then men said to him: Speak to us, sir.
To them he spoke this same syllable, da, and asked: Did you understand?
They said: We understood; you told us: Give (datta). Prajāpati said: Yes, you understood. ॥5.2.2॥
5.2.3: Then the demons said to him: Speak to us, sir.
To them he spoke this same syllable, da, and asked: Did you understand?
They said: We understood; you told us: Be compassionate (dayadhvam). Prajāpati said: Yes, you understood.
This very thing the divine voice, the thunder, repeats: da, da, da; that is, restrain yourselves, give, be compassionate.
Therefore one should learn these three: self-restraint, giving and compassion. ॥5.2.3॥
5.3.1: This is Prajāpati: the heart. This is Brahman; this is all.
Hṛdayam, the heart, is a word of three syllables.
Hṛ is one syllable: his own people and others bring (offerings) to him who knows thus.
Da is one syllable: his own people and others give to him who knows thus.
Yam is one syllable: he who knows thus goes to the heavenly world. ॥5.3.1॥
5.4.1: That (Brahman, the heart) was indeed just this: the true (satya) itself.

He who knows thus this great, adorable, first-born being, that the true is Brahman, conquers these worlds; and conquered in the same way is that one, his enemy, and he comes to nothing: he who knows thus this great, adorable, first-born being, that the true is Brahman; for the true indeed is Brahman. ॥5.4.1॥
5.5.1: In the beginning this was the waters alone. The waters brought forth the true (satya); the true is Brahman. Brahman brought forth Prajāpati, and Prajāpati the gods. Those gods worship the true alone. This word, satyam, has three syllables.
Sa is one syllable, ti one syllable, yam one syllable.
The first and the last syllables are the true; in the middle is the untrue. This untrue is held on both sides by the true, and so it becomes mostly the true.
The untrue does not harm one who knows thus. ॥5.5.1॥
5.5.2: That true is the sun yonder:

the person in this orb and the person in the right eye. Each of these two rests on the other: the one in the sun rests on the one in the eye through the rays, and the one in the eye on the one in the sun through the prāṇas. When he (who dwells in the body) is about to depart, he sees this orb quite clear, without rays; these rays no longer come back to him. ॥5.5.2॥
5.5.3: Of the person who is in this orb, bhūḥ is the head: the head is one, and this syllable is one; bhuvaḥ is the two arms: the arms are two, and these syllables are two; svaḥ is the two feet: the feet are two, and these syllables are two.
He who knows thus strikes down evil and leaves it behind. ॥5.5.3॥
5.5.4: Of the person who is in the right eye, bhūḥ is the head: the head is one, and this syllable is one; bhuvaḥ is the two arms: the arms are two, and these syllables are two; svaḥ is the two feet: the feet are two, and these syllables are two.
He who knows thus strikes down evil and leaves it behind. ॥5.5.4॥
5.6.1: This person is made of mind; light is his true being. He is within the heart, the size of a grain of rice or of barley. He is the ruler of all and the overlord of all; he governs all this, whatever there is. ॥5.6.1॥
5.7.1: Lightning is Brahman, they say. Lightning (vidyut) is so called because it cuts (vidāna) through (the darkness). He who knows thus, that lightning is Brahman, cuts down the evils that beset him.
5.8.1: One should worship speech as a cow.
She has four teats: the utterances svāhā, vaṣaṭ, hanta and svadhā. On two of her teats, svāhā and vaṣaṭ, the gods live; on hanta, men; on svadhā, the ancestors (pitṛs).
Prāṇa, the vital breath, is her bull; the mind is her calf. ॥5.8.1॥
5.9.1: This fire Vaiśvānara is the one within a person, by which the food that is eaten is digested.
This is its sound, which one hears on closing one's ears.
When he is about to depart, he does not hear this sound. ॥5.9.1॥
5.10.1: When a person departs from this world, he comes to the air. There it opens for him as wide as the hole of a chariot wheel; through that he climbs upward.
He comes to the sun. There it opens for him as wide as the hole of a lambara (a kind of drum); through that he climbs upward.
He comes to the moon. There it opens for him as wide as the hole of a kettledrum (dundubhi); through that he climbs upward.
He comes to a world without sorrow and without cold; there he dwells for endless years. ॥5.10.1॥
5.11.1: This indeed is the highest austerity: that one suffers when sick. He who knows thus wins the highest world. This indeed is the highest austerity: that, when he is dead, they carry him to the forest. He who knows thus wins the highest world. This indeed is the highest austerity: that, when he is dead, they lay him on the fire. He who knows thus wins the highest world. ॥5.11.1॥
5.12.1: Some say: Food is Brahman. That is not so, for without prāṇa, the vital breath, food rots. Some say: Prāṇa is Brahman. That is not so, for without food prāṇa dries up. But these two deities, becoming one, reach the highest state. On this, Prātṛda said to his father: What good could I do to one who knows thus, and what harm could I do him?
His father, stopping him with his hand, said: Not so, Prātṛda. Who reaches the highest state by the oneness of these two?
And he said this to him: vi. Food indeed is vi, for all these beings have entered into food.
Ram. Prāṇa indeed is ram, for all these beings delight in prāṇa.
Into him who knows thus all beings enter, and in him all beings delight. ॥5.12.1॥
5.13.1: The uktha (the chief hymn recited at the sacrifice): prāṇa, the vital breath, is the uktha, for prāṇa raises up all this. From him rises a heroic son who knows the uktha; he who knows thus wins union with the uktha (sāyujya) and a place in its world (salokatā). ॥5.13.1॥
5.13.2: The yajus: prāṇa indeed is the yajus, for in prāṇa all these beings are joined.
All beings are joined to him for his pre-eminence; he who knows thus wins union with the yajus and a place in its world. ॥5.13.2॥
5.13.3: The sāman: prāṇa indeed is the sāman, for in prāṇa all these beings come together.
All beings come together for him and serve his pre-eminence; he who knows thus wins union with the sāman and a place in its world. ॥5.13.3॥
5.13.4: The kṣatra (the ruling power): prāṇa indeed is the kṣatra, for prāṇa is indeed the kṣatra: prāṇa protects (trāyate) this (body) from wounds (kṣaṇitoḥ).
He attains the kṣatra that needs no other to protect it; he who knows thus wins union with the kṣatra and a place in its world. ॥5.13.4॥
5.14.1: Bhūmi (earth), antarikṣa (mid-region), dyaus (heaven): these are eight syllables; and one foot of the Gāyatrī has eight syllables. This (the three worlds) is that (first foot) of hers. He who knows this foot of hers thus wins as much as there is in these three worlds. ॥5.14.1॥
5.14.2: Ṛcaḥ, yajūṃṣi, sāmāni (the verses, the formulas, the chants): these are eight syllables; and one foot of the Gāyatrī has eight syllables.
This (the three Vedas) is that (second foot) of hers. He who knows this foot of hers thus wins as much as this threefold knowledge reaches. ॥5.14.2॥
5.14.3: Prāṇa, apāna, vyāna (the vital breaths): these are eight syllables; and one foot of the Gāyatrī has eight syllables. This (the breaths) is that (third foot) of hers. He who knows this foot of hers thus wins as much as there is that breathes. Now this is her fourth (turīya), visible foot, beyond the rajas (the worlds): he who shines yonder. What is the fourth is called turīya; the visible foot, for he is seen, as it were; beyond the rajas, for he shines over all the rajas, high above each of them. He who knows this foot of hers thus shines just so, with splendour and fame. ॥5.14.3॥
5.14.4: This Gāyatrī rests on that fourth, visible foot, beyond the rajas. That (foot) rests on the true (satya). The eye indeed is the true, for the eye is indeed the true. Therefore, if two should come now disputing, one saying: I saw, the other: I heard, we would believe the one who says: I saw.
That true rests on strength (bala). Prāṇa indeed is strength; it rests on prāṇa. Therefore they say: strength is mightier (ogīya) than the true. Thus this Gāyatrī rests within the body (adhyātma).
She protected the gayas. The prāṇas (the organs) indeed are the gayas; she protected the prāṇas. Because she protected (tatre) the gayas, she is named Gāyatrī.
That Sāvitrī which he (the teacher) teaches is this very one.
She protects the prāṇas of the one to whom he teaches her. ॥5.14.4॥
5.14.5: Some teach this Sāvitrī as the anuṣṭubh (verse), saying: Speech is the anuṣṭubh; we teach that speech.
One should not do so; one should teach the Gāyatrī itself as the Sāvitrī.
Even if one who knows thus accepts a great deal, as it were, that is not equal to even one foot of the Gāyatrī. ॥5.14.5॥
5.14.6: If one should accept these three worlds, full (of wealth), he would reach this first foot of hers.

And if one should accept as much as this threefold knowledge, he would reach this second foot of hers; and if one should accept as much as there is that breathes, he would reach this third foot of hers. But this fourth, visible foot of hers, beyond the rajas, he who shines yonder, is not to be reached by anything at all; and whence could anyone accept so much? ॥5.14.6॥
5.14.7: Her upasthāna (the worship in which one approaches her): O Gāyatrī, you are one-footed, two-footed, three-footed, four-footed; you are footless, for you are not reached.

Salutation to you, the fourth, visible foot, beyond the rajas! May so-and-so not obtain that! — so (one says) of the one he hates; or: May so-and-so's wish not prosper! That wish never prospers for him about whom one worships thus. Or: I have obtained that! ॥5.14.7॥
5.14.8: On this, Janaka Vaideha said to Buḍila Āśvatarāśvi: Ah! You called yourself a knower of the Gāyatrī; how is it, then, that you have become an elephant and carry (burdens)?
Buḍila said: For, O emperor, I did not know her mouth.

Janaka said: Fire indeed is her mouth. Even if they put a great deal on the fire, it burns it all; just so one who knows thus, even if he does a great deal of evil, consumes it all and becomes pure, clean, ageless and immortal. ॥5.14.8॥
5.15.1: The face of Truth is covered by a golden vessel.
O Pūṣan (the Sun, nourisher of all), uncover it, so that I, devoted to the Truth, may see it.
O Pūṣan, lone seer, Yama (controller of all), Sūrya, son of Prajāpati, spread apart your rays,
gather in your light. Your most blessed form I see.
That Person yonder — He am I.
I am immortal: let my breath go back to the air outside, and then let this body end in ashes.
Om! O mind (kratu), remember, remember what has been done; O mind, remember, remember what has been done.
O Agni, O god who knows the thoughts of all beings, lead us by the good path to wealth (the fruit of our deeds).
Keep from us the crooked sin. We offer you salutations again and again in words. ॥5.15.1॥
6.1.1: Om. He who knows the eldest and the best becomes the eldest and the best among his own people.
Prāṇa, the vital breath, is indeed the eldest and the best.
He who knows thus becomes the eldest and the best among his own people, and among those too among whom he wishes to be so. ॥6.1.1॥
6.1.2: He who knows the richest (vasiṣṭhā) becomes the richest among his own people.
He who knows thus becomes the richest among his own people, and among those too among whom he wishes to be so. ॥6.1.2॥
6.1.3: He who knows the firm ground (pratiṣṭhā) stands firm where the way is even, stands firm where it is hard.
The eye is indeed the firm ground, for it is with the eye that one stands firm both where the way is even and where it is hard.
He who knows thus stands firm where the way is even, stands firm where it is hard. ॥6.1.3॥
6.1.4: For him who knows fulfilment (sampad), whatever desire he desires is fulfilled.
The ear is indeed fulfilment, for it is in the ear that all these Vedas are attained.
For him who knows thus, whatever desire he desires is fulfilled. ॥6.1.4॥
6.1.5: He who knows the abode (āyatana) becomes the abode of his own people, the abode of people at large.
The mind is indeed the abode. He who knows thus becomes the abode of his own people, the abode of people at large. ॥6.1.5॥
6.1.6: He who knows procreation (prajāti) multiplies in offspring and cattle. Semen is indeed procreation.
He who knows thus multiplies in offspring and cattle. ॥6.1.6॥
6.1.7: These prāṇas (speech and the other organs), disputing among themselves, each claiming: I am the better, went to Brahman (Prajāpati) and said: Which of us is the richest (vasiṣṭha)?
Brahman said: The one of you on whose going out this body is thought the more wretched, he is the richest of you. ॥6.1.7॥
6.1.8: Having stayed away a year, it came back and said: How were you able to live without me?
The others said: As the mute live, not speaking with speech, but breathing with prāṇa, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, understanding with the mind and begetting with semen, so we lived.
6.1.9: Having stayed away a year, it came back and said: How were you able to live without me?
The others said: As the blind live, not seeing with the eye, but breathing with prāṇa, speaking with speech, hearing with the ear, understanding with the mind and begetting with semen, so we lived.
6.1.10: Having stayed away a year, it came back and said: How were you able to live without me?
The others said: As the deaf live, not hearing with the ear, but breathing with prāṇa, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, understanding with the mind and begetting with semen, so we lived.
6.1.11: Having stayed away a year, it came back and said: How were you able to live without me?

The others said: As the simple-minded live, not understanding with the mind, but breathing with prāṇa, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear and begetting with semen, so we lived.
6.1.12: Having stayed away a year, it came back and said: How were you able to live without me?

The others said: As the impotent live, not begetting with semen, but breathing with prāṇa, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear and understanding with the mind, so we lived.
6.1.13: Then prāṇa, about to go out — as a great, fine horse from Sindhu would tear up at one stroke the pegs that tether its feet — tore up these prāṇas in the same way.
They said: Revered sir, do not go out; we shall not be able to live without you.
Prāṇa said: Such as I am, then, pay me tribute (bali). They said: So be it. ॥6.1.13॥
6.1.14: Speech said: In that I am the richest, in that it is you who are the richest.
The eye said: In that I am the firm ground, in that it is you who are the firm ground. The ear said: In that I am fulfilment, in that it is you who are fulfilment.

The mind said: In that I am the abode, in that it is you who are the abode. Semen said: In that I am procreation, in that it is you who are procreation. Prāṇa said: Such as I am, then, what will be my food, and what my clothing?
They said: Whatever there is here, down to dogs, down to worms, down to insects and moths, that is your food; water is your clothing.
For him who knows thus this food of ana (prāṇa), nothing he eats is other than food, nothing he accepts is other than food.
Therefore the learned, versed in the Veda (śrotriyas), sip water when about to eat and sip water when they have eaten; they consider that by this they make that very food not naked. ॥6.1.14॥
6.2.1: Śvetaketu Āruṇeya came to the assembly of the Pañcālas.
He came up to Pravāhaṇa Jaivali, who was having himself waited on.
Pravāhaṇa looked up at him and said: Boy!
Śvetaketu answered: Sir! Pravāhaṇa asked: Has your father taught you? Śvetaketu said: Yes. ॥6.2.1॥
6.2.2: Pravāhaṇa asked: Do you know how these creatures, as they depart, go their different ways?
Do you know how they come back again to this world?
Do you know how that world is not filled up, though many go there again and again in this way? Again he said: No.
Do you know at which offering in the series, when it has been offered, the waters take on the voice of man, rise up and speak?

Do you know the means of reaching the path of the gods (devayāna) or the path of the fathers (pitṛyāṇa): by doing what people reach the path of the gods or the path of the fathers? For we have also heard the seer's word: I have heard of two paths for mortals, that of the fathers and that of the gods; by these two goes all this that moves — the two that lie between the father and the mother.
Śvetaketu said: I do not know even one of these. ॥6.2.2॥
6.2.3: Then the king invited him to stay; but the boy, paying no heed to the invitation, ran off.
He came to his father and said to him: So, sir, you told us before that we had been taught!
The father said: How so, my wise one?
Śvetaketu said: That so-called kṣatriya (rājanyabandhu) asked me five questions, and I do not know even one of them.
The father asked: Which are they? These, he said, and he quoted their opening words. ॥6.2.3॥
6.2.4: The father said: My dear, you must know this of me: whatever I knew, all of it I told you.
But come, let us go there; we two shall live with him as students (brahmacārins).
Śvetaketu said: You go yourself, sir.
Gautama (Āruṇi) came to where Pravāhaṇa Jaivali sat (in court).
The king had a seat brought for him and had water brought, and then made him the guest-offering (arghya).
Pravāhaṇa said to him: We give a boon to the revered Gautama. ॥6.2.4॥
6.2.5: Gautama said: This boon you have promised me; tell me the words you spoke in the boy's presence. ॥6.2.5॥
6.2.6: Pravāhaṇa said: That, Gautama, is among the boons of the gods; ask for one of the boons of men. ॥6.2.6॥
6.2.7: Gautama said: It is well known that I have gold, cows and horses, maidservants, retinues and clothing. Do not, sir, be ungenerous to us alone with what is great, endless and boundless.
Pravāhaṇa said: Then, Gautama, seek it in the proper way. Gautama said: I come to you, sir, as a pupil. With words alone, indeed, did the people of old come (to a teacher).
So he stayed there, having only declared that he came as a pupil. ॥6.2.7॥
6.2.8: Pravāhaṇa said: Do not hold it against us, Gautama, just as your grandfathers did not hold it against ours. As you know, before now this knowledge has never dwelt with any brāhmaṇa; but I will tell it to you, for when you speak like this, who could turn you away? ॥6.2.8॥
6.2.9: That world yonder (heaven), O Gautama, is indeed a fire.

Of this fire the sun itself is the fuel, the rays are the smoke, the day is the flame, the quarters are the embers, and the intermediate quarters are the sparks. In this very fire the gods offer faith; from that offering King Soma arises. ॥6.2.9॥
6.2.10: Parjanya, the god of rain, O Gautama, is indeed a fire.

Of this fire the year itself is the fuel, the clouds are the smoke, the lightning is the flame, the thunderbolt is the embers, and the rumblings of thunder are the sparks. In this very fire the gods offer King Soma; from that offering rain arises. ॥6.2.10॥
6.2.11: This world, O Gautama, is indeed a fire.

Of this fire the earth itself is the fuel, fire is the smoke, the night is the flame, the moon is the embers, and the stars are the sparks. In this very fire the gods offer rain; from that offering food arises. ॥6.2.11॥
6.2.12: Man, O Gautama, is indeed a fire.

Of this fire the open mouth itself is the fuel, prāṇa, the vital breath, is the smoke, speech is the flame, the eye is the embers, and the ear is the sparks. In this very fire the gods offer food; from that offering semen arises. ॥6.2.12॥
6.2.13: Woman, O Gautama, is indeed a fire.

Of this fire her generative organ itself is the fuel, the hair is the smoke, the vulva is the flame, what is done within is the embers, and the pleasures are the sparks. In this very fire the gods offer semen; from that offering man arises.
He lives for as long as he lives; then, when he dies — ॥6.2.13॥
6.2.14: Then they carry him to the fire.

For him the fire itself becomes the fire, the fuel the fuel, the smoke the smoke, the flame the flame, the embers the embers, the sparks the sparks. In this very fire the gods offer man; from that offering the man arises, shining in colour. ॥6.2.14॥
6.2.15: Those who know this thus, and those who in the forest worship with faith the True (satya), pass into the flame; from the flame into the day; from the day into the fortnight of the waxing moon; from the waxing fortnight into the six months when the sun travels north; from those months into the world of the gods; from the world of the gods into the sun; from the sun into the lightning. To them, once in the lightning, a person born of the mind comes and leads them to the worlds of Brahman. In those worlds of Brahman they dwell, exalted, for vast ages.
For them there is no return. ॥6.2.15॥
6.2.16: But those who win the worlds by sacrifice, gifts and austerity pass into the smoke; from the smoke into the night; from the night into the fortnight of the waning moon; from the waning fortnight into the six months when the sun travels south; from those months into the world of the fathers; from that world into the moon. Reaching the moon, they become food; and as (the priests) drink King Soma, making it swell and wane, so the gods there feed on them.

When that (work) of theirs is spent, they pass into this very space; from space into the air; from the air into rain; from rain into the earth. On reaching the earth they become food, and are offered once more in the fire that is man; then they are born in the fire that is woman; rising up again towards the worlds, they go round and round in just this way. But those who do not know these two paths become insects and moths and whatever biting creatures there are. ॥6.2.16॥
6.3.1: He who desires: May I attain greatness — in the northern course of the sun, on an auspicious day of the bright fortnight, having kept the upasad vow (living on milk alone) for twelve days, gathers in a cup or a bowl of udumbara wood all herbs, fruits and the rest; sweeps the ground around, smears it, sets the fire in place, strews (kuśa grass) around, prepares the ghee by the prescribed (household) procedure, and, under an asterism with a male name, sets the mantha (the herbs and fruits ground and stirred together) in the middle and offers (into the fire, saying):

O Jātavedas (Agni), as many gods as are in you, who turn crosswise (against him) and destroy a man's desires, to them I offer their share; may they, satisfied, satisfy me with all desires: svāhā (the call of offering).
She who lies crosswise (against him), thinking: I am the one who holds all back — you are she; you, the bringer of success, I worship with a stream of ghee.
6.3.2: Svāhā to the eldest, svāhā to the best: so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (the ghee clinging to the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to prāṇa (the vital breath), svāhā to the richest (vasiṣṭhā): so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to speech, svāhā to the firm ground (pratiṣṭhā): so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to the eye, svāhā to prosperity (sampad): so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to the ear, svāhā to the abode (āyatana): so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to the mind, svāhā to procreation (prajāti): so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to semen: so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha. ॥6.3.2॥
6.3.3: Svāhā to Agni: so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to Soma: so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Bhūḥ (earth), svāhā: so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Bhuvaḥ (the mid-space), svāhā: so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svaḥ (heaven), svāhā: so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, svāhā: so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to the brahman (the priestly power): so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to the kṣatra (the ruling power): so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to what has been: so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to what will be: so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to the universe: so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to the all: so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha.
Svāhā to Prajāpati: so saying he offers into the fire and pours what is left (on the ladle) into the mantha. ॥6.3.3॥
6.3.4: Then he touches it (the mantha, saying): You are moving, you are blazing, you are full, you are motionless, you are the one meeting-place (of all); you are the hiṃ that has been uttered, you are the hiṃ being uttered; you are the udgītha, you are being sung; you are the call that has been proclaimed, you are the call proclaimed in answer; you are blazing in the moist (cloud); you are pervading, you are the lord; you are food, you are light, you are the closing chant (nidhana), you are the gatherer who takes all into himself. ॥6.3.4॥
6.3.5: Then he lifts it (in its vessel, in his hand, saying): You know; we know your greatness.
He is the king, the ruler, the overlord; may he make me king, ruler, overlord. ॥6.3.5॥
6.3.6: Then he sips it, saying: That excellent (radiance) of Savitṛ —
The winds blow honey for him who keeps to the right (ṛta); the rivers pour honey.
May the plants be sweet to us.
We meditate on the radiance of the god. Sweet be the night and the dawns; sweet be the region of the earth.
Sweet be the tree to us; sweet be the sun.
May the cows be sweet to us.
He recites the whole Sāvitrī and all the madhumatī (honey) verses, and says: May I indeed become all this.
Saying at the end: Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, svāhā, he drinks (the rest), washes his hands, and lies down behind the fire with his head to the east.
At dawn he worships the sun, saying: You are the one lotus of the quarters; may I become the one lotus among men.
Then, going back the way he came, he sits behind the fire and recites the line of teachers (vaṃśa). ॥6.3.6॥
6.3.7: Uddālaka Āruṇi told this (mantha) to his pupil Yājñavalkya Vājasaneya and said: Even if one were to pour it on a dry stump, branches would spring from it and leaves would sprout. ॥6.3.7॥
6.3.8: This very (mantha) Yājñavalkya Vājasaneya told to his pupil Madhuka Paiṅgya, and said: Even if one were to pour it on a dry stump, branches would spring from it and leaves would sprout. ॥6.3.8॥
6.3.9: This very (mantha) Madhuka Paiṅgya told to his pupil Cūla Bhāgavitti, and said: Even if one were to pour it on a dry stump, branches would spring from it and leaves would sprout. ॥6.3.9॥
6.3.10: This very (mantha) Cūla Bhāgavitti told to his pupil Jānaki Āyasthūṇa, and said: Even if one were to pour it on a dry stump, branches would spring from it and leaves would sprout. ॥6.3.10॥
6.3.11: This very (mantha) Jānaki Āyasthūṇa told to his pupil Satyakāma Jābāla, and said: Even if one were to pour it on a dry stump, branches would spring from it and leaves would sprout. ॥6.3.11॥
6.3.12: This very (mantha) Satyakāma Jābāla told to his pupils, and said: Even if one were to pour it on a dry stump, branches would spring from it and leaves would sprout.
One should not tell it to anyone who is neither a son nor a pupil. ॥6.3.12॥
6.3.13: Four things are of udumbara wood: the ladle of udumbara, the bowl of udumbara, the fuel of udumbara, the two stirring-rods of udumbara.

There are ten kinds of grain grown in the village: rice and barley, sesame and black gram (māṣa), the millets aṇu and priyaṅgu, wheat, lentils, khalva (a bean) and khalakula (horse gram). These he grinds and steeps in curd, honey and ghee, and he offers the ghee (into the fire). ॥6.3.13॥
6.4.1: Of all these beings the earth is the essence; of the earth, the waters; of the waters, the plants; of the plants, the flowers; of the flowers, the fruits; of the fruits, man; of man, the semen. ॥6.4.1॥
6.4.2: Prajāpati thought: Come, let me make a firm ground (pratiṣṭhā) for it (the semen). He created woman.

Having created her, he approached her below (in union); therefore a man should approach a woman below. From his own self he raised this pressing-stone that juts forward, his organ, and with it he united with her. ॥6.4.2॥
6.4.3: Her organ is the altar, her hair the sacred grass, her skin the hide of the soma-pressing; in the middle is the kindled fire; and those two labia are the two boards of the soma-press (adhiṣavaṇa).

As great as the world of one who sacrifices with the Vājapeya is, so great is the world of him who has intercourse knowing thus; he draws to himself the merit of these women. But he who has intercourse without knowing this, women draw his merit to themselves. ॥6.4.3॥
6.4.4: Knowing this, Uddālaka Āruṇi said, knowing this, Nāka Maudgalya said, knowing this, Kumārahārita said: Many mortals, brāhmaṇas by birth alone, depart from this world bereft of virility and without merit: those who have intercourse without knowing this.
Much or little, this semen may be spilled, whether one is asleep or awake. ॥6.4.4॥
6.4.5: He should touch it, or address it with these words: The semen of mine that has fallen today on the earth, that has run into the plants, into the waters,
this semen I here take back. May virility come back to me, brightness again, good fortune again.
May the fire and the fire-altars (dhiṣṇya) again be set each in its place. So saying, he should take it with the ring finger and the thumb and rub it between his breasts or between his brows. ॥6.4.5॥
6.4.6: And if he should see himself (his reflection) in water, he should address it with these words: In me be brightness, virility, fame, wealth, merit.

She indeed is the glory (śrī) among women who has put off her soiled clothes (at the end of her monthly course); therefore, when she has put off her soiled clothes and is glorious, he should go to her and invite her. ॥6.4.6॥
6.4.7: If she will not give herself to him, he may freely buy her over (with gifts); if she still will not give herself to him, he may freely beat her with a stick or with his hand and prevail over her, saying: With virility, with glory, I take your glory from you. And she becomes without glory. ॥6.4.7॥
6.4.8: If she gives herself to him, (he says): With virility, with glory, I place glory in you. And the two of them become glorious. ॥6.4.8॥
6.4.9: She of whom he wishes: May she love me — placing his organ in her, joining mouth to mouth and touching her organ, he should repeat: From every limb you come into being; from the heart you are born.
You are the essence of the limbs: as one pierced by a poisoned arrow, make this woman, so-and-so, mad for me. ॥6.4.9॥
6.4.10: And she of whom he wishes: May she not conceive — placing his organ in her and joining mouth to mouth, he should breathe out into her and then draw the breath back, saying: With virility, with semen, I take the semen back from you. And she remains without seed. ॥6.4.10॥
6.4.11: And she of whom he wishes: May she conceive — placing his organ in her and joining mouth to mouth, he should draw in the breath and then breathe out into her, saying: With virility, with semen, I place semen in you. And she becomes pregnant. ॥6.4.11॥
6.4.12: Now, if a man's wife has a lover and he hates him, he should set fire in an unbaked vessel, spread a bed of reeds in reverse order, and in that fire offer, in reverse order, these reed-tips smeared with ghee, saying: You have made an offering in my kindled fire: your prāṇa and apāna (the vital breath and the downward breath) I take from you, so-and-so.
You have made an offering in my kindled fire: your sons and your cattle I take from you, so-and-so.
You have made an offering in my kindled fire: your sacrifices and your good works I take from you, so-and-so.
You have made an offering in my kindled fire: your hope and your expectation I take from you, so-and-so.
The man cursed by a brāhmaṇa who knows this departs from this world bereft of virility and without merit.
Therefore, with the wife of a śrotriya (a brāhmaṇa learned in the Veda) who knows this, one should not seek dalliance; for one who knows this becomes an enemy. ॥6.4.12॥
6.4.13: Now, when the wife of a man has her monthly course, for three days she should not drink from a bronze vessel, nor should a Śūdra man or a Śūdra woman touch her; at the end of the three nights, having bathed, she should put on new clothes, and he should have her pound rice. ॥6.4.13॥
6.4.14: He who wishes that a son of fair complexion be born to him, that he study one Veda and that he live the full span of life, should have rice boiled in milk; husband and wife should both eat it with ghee, and they are then able to beget such a son. ॥6.4.14॥
6.4.15: Now he who wishes that a son brown and tawny in colour be born to him, that he study two Vedas and that he live the full span of life, should have rice cooked with curds; husband and wife should both eat it with ghee, and they are then able to beget such a son. ॥6.4.15॥
6.4.16: Now he who wishes that a son dark in colour and with reddish eyes be born to him, that he study three Vedas and that he live the full span of life, should have rice cooked in water; husband and wife should both eat it with ghee, and they are then able to beget such a son. ॥6.4.16॥
6.4.17: Now he who wishes that a learned daughter be born to him and that she live the full span of life should have rice cooked with sesame; husband and wife should both eat it with ghee, and they are then able to beget such a daughter. ॥6.4.17॥
6.4.18: Now he who wishes that a son be born to him who is learned, renowned, one who goes into assemblies, a speaker of words that people long to hear, that he study all the Vedas and that he live the full span of life, should have rice cooked with meat; husband and wife should both eat it with ghee, and they are then able to beget such a son.
The meat is to be that of a bull in its prime or of an older bull. ॥6.4.18॥
6.4.19: Then, early in the morning, having prepared the ghee by the procedure of the sthālīpāka, the rice cooked in a pot for an offering, he takes portions of the sthālīpāka and offers them, saying: To Agni svāhā (the call of offering); to Anumati svāhā; to the god Savitṛ, whose impulse is true, svāhā. Having offered them, he takes up what remains and eats it.
Having eaten, he gives the rest to the other, his wife.

He washes his hands, fills a vessel with water and with it sprinkles her three times, saying: Rise from here, Viśvāvasu (a gandharva); seek another, a young maiden; let the wife be joined with her husband. ॥6.4.19॥
6.4.20: Then he approaches her, saying: I am ama (prāṇa), you are sā (speech); you are sā, I am ama; I am the Sāman, you are the Ṛk; I am heaven, you are the earth.
Come, let us join together; let us place the seed together, to gain a male child, a son. ॥6.4.20॥
6.4.21: Then he parts her thighs, saying: Part, heaven and earth.

Having placed his organ in her and joined mouth to mouth, he strokes her three times from the head downward, saying: May Viṣṇu make the womb ready; may Tvaṣṭṛ shape the forms; may Prajāpati pour in; may Dhātṛ place the embryo in you.
Place the embryo, O Sinīvālī; place the embryo, O broad-tressed one.
May the two Aśvins, the gods garlanded with lotuses, place the embryo in you. ॥6.4.21॥
6.4.22: There are two golden fire-sticks, with which the Aśvins churned out fire; that embryo of yours we invoke, to be born in the tenth month.
As the earth holds fire in her womb, as heaven is pregnant with Indra, as the wind is the embryo of the quarters, so I place an embryo in you, so-and-so. ॥6.4.22॥
6.4.23: He sprinkles with water the woman about to give birth, saying: As the wind stirs a lotus pond on every side,
even so may your embryo stir and come out together with its membrane.
This pen of Indra has been made, with its bolt and its fence.
O Indra, drive it out, together with the child and the afterbirth. ॥6.4.23॥
6.4.24: When the son is born, he kindles the fire, places him in his lap, mixes curds and ghee in a bronze vessel and offers portions of the curds and ghee one by one, saying: In this son may I, thriving in my own home, support a thousand.
May there be no break in his line, in offspring or in cattle. Svāhā.
The prāṇas, the vital breaths, that are in me I offer in you with my mind. Svāhā.
Whatever in this rite I have done in excess, or whatever I have done too little here,
may Agni, who knows, the maker of the right offering, make it rightly sacrificed and well offered for us. Svāhā. ॥6.4.24॥
6.4.25: Then, putting his mouth to the child's right ear, he says three times: Speech, speech. Then he mixes curds, honey and ghee and feeds it to him with gold, directly, with nothing in between.
He says: I place bhūḥ in you, I place bhuvaḥ in you, I place svaḥ in you; bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ: all I place in you. ॥6.4.25॥
6.4.26: Then he names him, saying: You are Veda.
6.4.27: Then, handing the child to his mother, he puts him to the breast, saying: That breast of yours which is ever full, which brings joy, which bestows treasures, which wins wealth, which gives good gifts, by which you nourish all things worth choosing, O Sarasvatī, make it here for him to drink from. ॥6.4.27॥
6.4.28: Then he addresses the child's mother with a mantra:
You are Ilā, daughter of Mitra and Varuṇa; heroic woman, she has borne a hero.
Be blessed with heroes, you who have blessed us with a hero.
People say of such a son: Ah, you have become greater than your father; ah, you have become greater than your grandfather.
Ah, by prosperity, renown and the lustre of sacred knowledge he has reached the highest summit, he who is born as the son of a brāhmaṇa who knows thus. ॥6.4.28॥
6.5.1: Pautimāṣīputra received this teaching from Kātyāyanīputra, Kātyāyanīputra from Gautamīputra, Gautamīputra from Bhāradvājīputra, Bhāradvājīputra from Pārāśarīputra, Pārāśarīputra from Aupasvastīputra, Aupasvastīputra from Pārāśarīputra, Pārāśarīputra from Kātyāyanīputra, Kātyāyanīputra from Kauśikīputra, Kauśikīputra from Ālambīputra and from Vaiyāghrapadīputra, Vaiyāghrapadīputra from Kāṇvīputra and from Kāpīputra, Kāpīputra ॥6.5.1॥
6.5.2: from Ātreyīputra, Ātreyīputra from Gautamīputra, Gautamīputra from Bhāradvājīputra, Bhāradvājīputra from Pārāśarīputra, Pārāśarīputra from Vātsīputra, Vātsīputra from Pārāśarīputra, Pārāśarīputra from Vārkāruṇīputra, Vārkāruṇīputra from Vārkāruṇīputra, Vārkāruṇīputra from Ārtabhāgīputra, Ārtabhāgīputra from Śauṅgīputra, Śauṅgīputra from Sāṅkṛtīputra, Sāṅkṛtīputra from Ālambāyanīputra, Ālambāyanīputra from Ālambīputra, Ālambīputra from Jāyantīputra, Jāyantīputra from Māṇḍūkāyanīputra, Māṇḍūkāyanīputra from Māṇḍūkīputra, Māṇḍūkīputra from Śāṇḍilīputra, Śāṇḍilīputra from Rāthītarīputra, Rāthītarīputra from Bhālukīputra, Bhālukīputra from the two Krauñcikīputras, the two Krauñcikīputras from Vaidabhṛtīputra, Vaidabhṛtīputra from Kārśakeyīputra, Kārśakeyīputra from Prācīnayogīputra, Prācīnayogīputra from Sāñjīvīputra, Sāñjīvīputra from Prāśnīputra Āsurivāsin, Prāśnīputra from Āsurāyaṇa, Āsurāyaṇa from Āsuri, Āsuri ॥6.5.2॥
6.5.3: from Yājñavalkya, Yājñavalkya from Uddālaka, Uddālaka from Aruṇa, Aruṇa from Upaveśi, Upaveśi from Kuśri, Kuśri from Vājaśravas, Vājaśravas from Jihvāvat Bādhyoga, Jihvāvat Bādhyoga from Asita Vārṣagaṇa, Asita Vārṣagaṇa from Harita Kaśyapa, Harita Kaśyapa from Śilpa Kaśyapa, Śilpa Kaśyapa from Kaśyapa Naidhruvi, Kaśyapa Naidhruvi from Vāc, Vāc from Ambhiṇī, Ambhiṇī from Āditya. These white Yajus formulas, which come from Āditya, are made known by Yājñavalkya Vājasaneya. ॥6.5.3॥
6.5.4: The line is the same as far as Sāñjīvīputra. Sāñjīvīputra received it from Māṇḍūkāyani, Māṇḍūkāyani from Māṇḍavya, Māṇḍavya from Kautsa, Kautsa from Māhitthi, Māhitthi from Vāmakakṣāyaṇa, Vāmakakṣāyaṇa from Śāṇḍilya, Śāṇḍilya from Vātsya, Vātsya from Kuśri, Kuśri from Yajñavacas Rājastambāyana, Yajñavacas Rājastambāyana from Tura Kāvaṣeya, Tura Kāvaṣeya from Prajāpati, Prajāpati from Brahman. Brahman is self-existent.
